recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Roasted Chicken with Herbs and Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean Roasted Chicken is presented on a clean, white round porcelain plate. A golden-brown roasted chicken thigh is the focal point. Surrounding it are rustic chunks of roasted potato, their edges slightly crisped. Bright red, bursting cherry tomatoes are scattered among the potatoes. Vivid green broccoli florets, tender-crisp, are nestled alongside the main components. The dish is lightly drizzled with pan juices. Fresh chopped parsley adds a vibrant green garnish. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, with a folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors, creating an inviting, approachable restaurant aesthetic. The composition is balanced, showcasing quality ingredients and refined execution.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to absorb pan juices.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Wash potatoes. Cut larger new potatoes into halves or quarters. Keep smaller ones whole.
In a large bowl, combine potatoes, 30 ml olive oil, half the minced garlic, 3 g oregano, 3 g salt, and 1 g black pepper. Toss to coat.
Spread seasoned potatoes in a single layer on a large baking tray.
Roast for 20 minutes.
While potatoes roast, pat chicken thighs dry. In the same bowl, toss chicken with remaining olive oil, garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper.
After 20 minutes, remove tray from oven. Add chicken thighs and cherry tomatoes to the tray with the potatoes. Pour chicken broth over vegetables.
Return to oven. Roast for another 20-25 minutes. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F).
Steam broccoli florets until tender-crisp, about 5-7 minutes.
Remove tray from oven. Let chicken rest 5 minutes.
Serve chicken, potatoes, and tomatoes with steamed broccoli. Garnish with fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Cuban-Style Shredded Beef
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of rich, reddish-brown shredded beef is piled centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The beef, tender from slow braising, glistens with its savory tomato-based sauce. Interspersed throughout the shredded beef are vibrant green bell pepper strips and thin slivers of red onion, cooked soft but still holding their form. A few bright red chili flakes are scattered over the top for a subtle visual pop. The dish is garnished with fresh, bright green cilantro leaves, adding a touch of freshness. A crisp lime wedge sits beside the beef. The plate is set on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a small white bowl of fluffy white rice and a white cotton napkin. Natural, even light illuminates the scene, creating a professional yet inviting atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with white rice and black beans.
Offer warm tortillas or plantains on the side.

ingredients.name: Beef chuck roast or flank steak
Serrano chili, finely diced (seeds optional for less heat)

instructions: Pat beef dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef from pot. Set aside.
Add sliced onion and bell peppers to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Stir in minced garlic and diced serrano chili. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, beef broth, Worcestershire sauce, cumin, oregano, and bay leaves.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover pot tightly.
Braise for 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Check periodically to ensure liquid does not evaporate too much; add a splash of water or broth if needed.
Remove beef from pot. Shred with two forks.
Discard bay leaves from sauce. Simmer sauce over medium heat for 10-15 minutes, or until slightly thickened.
Return shredded beef to the sauce. Stir to combine. Season with additional salt and pepper if needed.
Garnish with fresh cilantro. Serve hot with lime wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Skillet Roasted Chicken and Potatoes with Cheesy Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Skillet Roasted Chicken and Potatoes with Cheesy Tomatoes is presented directly in a well-seasoned cast iron skillet. A golden-brown, whole roasted chicken thigh sits centrally, its crispy skin glistening. Around the chicken, roasted potato wedges display a light brown crust and tender interior. Scattered among them are vibrant red, halved cherry tomatoes, soft, caramelized thick onion slices, and whole smashed garlic cloves. A generous layer of melted, bubbly mozzarella cheese covers the tomatoes and onions, creating an inviting, gooey texture. The dish is garnished simply with fresh green chopped parsley, adding a pop of color. The skillet rests on a rustic, worn wooden dining table. A simple white ceramic plate is placed to the side, ready for serving. A casually draped linen napkin and a slice of crusty bread complete the homely, comforting scene. Warm, natural kitchen lighting illuminates the dish from above, highlighting its textures and inviting colors.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with half the salt, pepper, and oregano.
Wash potatoes. Cut potatoes into 2 cm wedges.
Peel onion. Cut onion into thick 2 cm slices.
Smash garlic cloves with the side of a knife.
Halve cherry tomatoes.
In a large oven-safe skillet or roasting pan, toss potato wedges with 30 ml olive oil, remaining salt, pepper, and oregano.
Place seasoned chicken thighs, skin-side up, among potatoes in the skillet.
Roast for 25 minutes. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C.
Remove skillet from oven. Add onion slices, smashed garlic, and halved cherry tomatoes to the skillet. Drizzle with remaining 30 ml olive oil.
Return to oven. Roast for another 15-20 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through and vegetables are tender.
Sprinkle shredded mozzarella cheese over the tomatoes and onions. Return to oven for 5 minutes, until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
Serve directly from the skillet with slices of crusty bread.

recipes.recipe_name: Arepas Rellenas con Pollo y Aguacate
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown, pan-fried and baked arepa sits centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The arepa is carefully sliced open, revealing a generous, vibrant filling of creamy, roughly mashed avocado mixed with tender, shredded white chicken. Flecks of bright green cilantro and finely diced red onion are visible within the filling, adding color and texture. A crisp lime wedge rests beside the arepa, ready for squeezing. The overall presentation is inviting and authentic, highlighting the arepa's warm, inviting color and the fresh, rich filling. The plate is set on a simple wooden surface with a folded white cotton napkin to the side, under soft, natural lighting. The scene is uncluttered, focusing entirely on the appetizing, culturally rich main course.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while arepas are warm.
Often accompanied by aji (Colombian hot sauce) on the side.
Can be enjoyed for breakfast, lunch, or a light dinner.
instructions: Place chicken breast in a pot. Cover with water and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken, let cool slightly, then shred into fine pieces.
In a medium bowl, mash avocados with a fork. Add diced red onion, chopped cilantro, lime juice, mayonnaise, salt, and pepper. Mix well to combine. Fold in the shredded chicken.
In a large bowl, combine masarepa, warm water, and salt. Mix with your hands until a soft, smooth dough forms. Knead for 2-3 minutes.
Divide the dough into 8 equal portions. Roll each portion into a ball, then flatten into a disc approximately 10 cm in diameter and 1.5 cm thick.
Heat vegetable oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Pan-fry arepas for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and a crust forms.
Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Transfer pan-fried arepas to a baking sheet. Bake for 15 minutes until fully cooked through and slightly puffed.
Carefully slice each warm arepa horizontally, creating a pocket. Do not cut completely through.
Generously fill each arepa pocket with the chicken and avocado mixture. Serve immediately.
traditional_techniques: Kneading masarepa dough to achieve proper texture
Pan-frying then baking/grilling for a crispy exterior and soft interior

recipes.recipe_name: Bell Pepper and Tomato Salad with Orange-Mustard Vinaigrette
recipes.visual_description: A generous portion of colorful Bell Pepper and Tomato Salad is presented on a simple, well-used ceramic dinner plate. Roasted bell pepper strips, in shades of red, yellow, and orange, are scattered among diced crimson tomatoes and thinly sliced ruby-red onion half-rings. Bright orange segments glisten, adding a pop of citrus. The vegetables are lightly coated in a golden-yellow orange-mustard vinaigrette, which subtly pools at the bottom of the plate. Textures are varied: soft roasted peppers, juicy tomatoes, crisp onion, and tender orange. The salad is casually arranged, allowing components to overlap naturally, evoking a homely, unpretentious feel. The plate sits on a warm, rustic wooden dining table, under soft, inviting kitchen light, with a casually placed cloth napkin nearby.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Slice bell peppers into 1 cm strips. Toss with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Spread bell peppers on a baking tray. Roast for 20-25 minutes until tender and slightly charred. Let cool.
Dice tomatoes into 1.5 cm cubes.
Thinly slice red onion into half-rings.
Cut oranges into segments (supremes) over a bowl to catch juice. Reserve juice for dressing.
In a small bowl, whisk together Dijon mustard, reserved orange juice, chicken stock, salt, and pepper.
Slowly drizzle in 60ml olive oil while whisking constantly until the dressing is emulsified.
In a large bowl, combine roasted bell pepper strips, diced tomatoes, thinly sliced red onion, and orange segments.
Pour dressing over the vegetables. Toss gently to coat all ingredients.
Arrange mixed salad greens on a platter or individual plates. Spoon the dressed bell pepper and tomato mixture over the greens.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Rigatoni with Italian Sausage and Basil Tomato Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Rigatoni with Italian Sausage and Basil Tomato Sauce is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The al dente rigatoni noodles are coated in a rich, rustic red tomato sauce, interspersed with golden-brown, crumbled Italian sausage chunks. Vibrant green fresh basil leaves are scattered throughout, with a few whole leaves artfully placed on top. A generous dusting of freshly grated white Parmesan cheese completes the dish. The overall color palette is warm and inviting: deep red, earthy brown, bright green, and creamy white. Textures are varied, from the firm pasta and tender sausage to the soft sauce and fresh herbs. The plate is well-proportioned, allowing for moderate negative space around the food. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, a grey cotton napkin beside the plate, and traditional silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, creating a professional yet approachable bistro ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add Italian sausage, breaking it apart with a spoon. Cook until browned and cooked through, about 8-10 minutes. Remove sausage with a slotted spoon; set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return cooked sausage to the sauce. Stir well. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes.
While sauce simmers, cook rigatoni according to package directions in salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve 120ml pasta water.
Drain pasta. Add pasta to the sauce. Add half of the chopped basil and half of the grated Parmesan.
Toss to combine. Add reserved pasta water as needed to reach desired consistency.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining fresh basil leaves and grated Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoky Chipotle Chicken and Brown Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a generous, naturally mounded portion of fluffy brown rice infused with smoky chipotle and rich chicken stock. Tender, golden-brown seared chicken thigh pieces, cut into rustic chunks, are nestled invitingly within and atop the rice, displaying a crisp exterior. Vibrant diced red bell peppers and finely minced cilantro sprigs are scattered throughout, adding pops of color and freshness. Each serving is crowned with a perfectly fried egg, its sunny-side-up yolk glistening, ready to meld into the dish. A fresh lime wedge rests beside the rice. The setting features a simple wooden table, a cotton napkin, and warm, natural lighting, highlighting the dish's inviting and abundant appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping.
Offer extra lime wedges for fresh acidity.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large, deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs until golden brown on all sides. Cook chicken to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the skillet. Reduce heat to medium.
Add diced onion and red bell pepper. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add brown rice to the skillet. Stir for 2 minutes to coat the rice.
Stir in chipotle chiles and adobo sauce. Pour in chicken stock.
Bring liquid to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover the skillet tightly.
Simmer for 30 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
While rice cooks, fry the eggs sunny-side up.
Once rice is cooked, return chicken thighs to the skillet. Fluff the rice with a fork. Mix in half of the fresh cilantro.
Serve individual portions of rice and chicken. Top each with a fried egg and remaining fresh cilantro. Serve with a lime wedge.
notes: Adjust chipotle chiles to desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato & Chicken Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Fermented Tomato & Chicken Pasta is presented on a handcrafted, cream-toned ceramic plate. The rigatoni, cooked al dente, is generously coated in a rich, rustic deep-red tomato sauce, studded with tender pieces of shredded chicken. A whole, braised chicken thigh, with its skin a golden-brown, rests naturally on top of the pasta, showcasing its tender texture. Scattered over the dish are small, irregular pieces of crispy, golden-brown chicken skin cracklings, adding a textural contrast. Fresh, vibrant green basil leaves are torn and sprinkled over the top, providing a pop of color and freshness. The plating is minimalist, allowing the natural colors and textures of the ingredients to shine. The background is a clean, light reclaimed wood surface with an undyed linen napkin in natural beige. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish, highlighting its organic beauty. The scene is uncluttered, emphasizing the sustainable and ingredient-focused nature of the meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
Offer crusty artisanal bread to soak up the rich sauce.
instructions: Prepare fermented tomatoes (at least 5 days in advance): Wash and roughly chop 500g ripe tomatoes. Place in a clean jar. Dissolve 15g sea salt in 500ml non-chlorinated water to make brine. Pour brine over tomatoes, ensuring they are fully submerged. Seal jar loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 5-7 days, burping daily, until tangy. Refrigerate when ready.
Separate chicken skin from thighs. Cut skin into small squares. Set thighs aside.
Render chicken skin: Place skin squares in a cold pan. Cook over medium-low heat until crispy and golden, about 10-15 minutes. Remove cracklings. Drain excess fat, reserving 15ml for cooking.

Sear chicken thighs: Heat reserved chicken fat or 15ml olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, until golden brown, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3 minutes. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Make chicken bone broth: Place chicken bones from thighs into a small pot. Add 1 L non-chlorinated water. Simmer gently for 30-45 minutes. Strain broth. Set aside.
Sauté aromatics: Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the large pot. Sauté diced onion until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Prepare tomato sauce: Crush fresh tomatoes by hand into the pot. Add fermented tomatoes and their brine. Stir in dried oregano. Bring to a simmer.

Braise chicken: Return seared chicken thighs to the sauce. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged. Cover and simmer over low heat for 30 minutes, or until chicken reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature and is tender. Remove chicken from sauce. Shred meat from bones. Discard bones or save for more broth. Keep shredded chicken warm.
Cook pasta: While chicken braises, cook rigatoni according to package directions in salted water until al dente. Reserve 120ml pasta water. Drain pasta.

Finish sauce: Add reserved chicken broth to the tomato sauce. Simmer gently. Stir in shredded chicken. Add grated Bel Paese cheese to the sauce, stirring until melted and creamy. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Combine: Add drained pasta to the sauce. Toss to coat evenly. Add a splash of reserved pasta water if needed for desired consistency.
Plate: Serve pasta in individual bowls. Top with fresh basil leaves. Scatter crispy chicken skin cracklings over each portion.
notes: The fermented tomatoes require preparation several days in advance. This step is key for flavor and eco-conscious practice.
Save chicken bones to make a flavorful broth, contributing to a zero-waste kitchen.
Adjust the amount of fermented tomato brine to control the tanginess of the sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Fermented Sourdough Crust, Dill Noodles & Pickled Cucumber
recipes.visual_description: A single seared chicken breast, golden-brown from its sourdough breadcrumb crust, rests on a matte white ceramic plate. Beside it, a loose nest of pale yellow noodles, tossed with finely chopped green dill, occupies the center. Thin, translucent ribbons of quick-pickled cucumber, a vibrant light green, are artfully draped around the chicken and noodles, adding delicate contrast. The arrangement is organic and clean, with ample negative space. The chicken offers a crisp exterior. The noodles are soft with bright green dill. The cucumber ribbons provide a smooth, fresh look. A few small, fresh dill sprigs garnish sparingly. The plate sits on a light, reclaimed wood surface. A natural beige linen napkin is folded simply. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish, highlighting textures. A subtle, out-of-focus green plant element is visible in the background.
instructions: Prepare Quick-Pickled Cucumber: Thinly slice 300g English cucumber into ribbons. Combine 125ml water, 125ml white vinegar, 15g granulated sugar, and 5g salt in a bowl. Submerge cucumber ribbons. Let sit for 30 minutes.
Prepare Fermented Sourdough Breadcrumbs: In a shallow dish, combine 100g sourdough breadcrumbs with 15ml olive oil, a pinch of salt, a pinch of black pepper, and 10g finely chopped fresh dill.
Cook Noodles: Boil 300g noodles according to package directions until al dente. Drain. Toss with 15ml olive oil and 20g finely chopped fresh dill. Keep warm.
Prepare Chicken: Pat 4 boneless, skinless chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and black pepper. Lightly dredge chicken breasts in the seasoned sourdough breadcrumbs, pressing to adhere firmly.

Sear Chicken: Heat a large pan over medium-high heat. Add a small amount of olive oil. Sear chicken breasts for 6-8 minutes per side, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove from pan, let rest 5 minutes.

Plate: Create a noodle nest on each of 4 plates. Place one seared chicken breast beside the noodle nest. Arrange quick-pickled cucumber ribbons around the chicken and noodles. Garnish with fresh dill sprigs.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing stale bread for crumbs.
Cucumber peels can be used for infused water or composted.

recipes.recipe_name: Sausage and Ricotta Stuffed Lumaconi
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Sausage and Ricotta Stuffed Lumaconi is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, showcasing a refined yet approachable elegance. Two large, plump lumaconi shells, generously stuffed with a creamy ricotta and crumbled Italian sausage filling, rest partially submerged in a rich, vibrant red marinara sauce. The pasta shells exhibit a tender, al dente texture, with a slight golden-brown char on exposed edges from baking. The filling, a creamy white with flecks of savory brown sausage, peeks from the pasta openings. A light dusting of melted, golden-brown Parmigiano Reggiano coats the top of the shells and sauce. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are artfully scattered as a garnish, providing a pop of color and freshness. The overall composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. The dish is set on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish’s textures and colors against a soft, blurred modern bistro background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Lightly grease a 23x33 cm baking dish.

Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add lumaconi pasta. Cook pasta until al dente, about 2 minutes less than package directions. Drain well. Rinse with cold water to prevent sticking.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add crumbled Italian sausage to the skillet. Cook, breaking up large pieces, until browned and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Drain excess fat.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Remove skillet from heat. Transfer sausage mixture to a large bowl. Let cool slightly.
Add ricotta cheese, 50 g of grated Parmigiano Reggiano, and half of the chopped fresh basil to the sausage mixture. Season with salt and pepper. Mix until just combined.
Pour half of the marinara sauce into the prepared baking dish. Spread evenly.
Carefully stuff each cooked lumaconi shell with the sausage-ricotta filling. Arrange stuffed shells in a single layer over the marinara sauce in the baking dish.
Pour remaining marinara sauce over the stuffed shells. Ensure most shells are covered.
Sprinkle remaining 50 g of Parmigiano Reggiano over the top.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until sauce is bubbly and cheese is melted and lightly golden. If browning too quickly, cover with foil.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with remaining fresh basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Pasta with Bresaola, Rocket, and Cherry Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pasta with Bresaola, Rocket, and Cherry Tomatoes is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The cooked pasta, such as tagliatelle, is loosely twirled and piled naturally in the center. Thinly sliced bresaola, with its deep ruby red color, is draped casually over the pasta strands. Halved, vibrant red cherry tomatoes are scattered throughout the dish, alongside fresh, dark green rocket leaves. A light sheen of olive oil coats the ingredients. The textures are varied: soft pasta, delicate bresaola, slightly burst tomatoes, and crisp rocket. The plate sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. A simple metal fork rests beside the plate. The background shows a hint of a cloth napkin and possibly a blurred glass of water, evoking a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere. Lighting is warm and natural, highlighting the food's inviting appearance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up any remaining sauce.
Pair with a light red wine like Valpolicella or a crisp white wine.
Offer a bowl of freshly grated Parmesan cheese at the table for individual preference.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 125 ml of pasta water before draining.
While pasta cooks, halve the cherry tomatoes. Thinly slice garlic cloves.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add sliced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Add halved cherry tomatoes to the pan. Cook for 3-4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes soften slightly and release juices.
Drain pasta. Add cooked pasta to the pan with tomatoes and garlic. Add rocket. Toss to combine.
Add bresaola slices to the pasta. Pour in reserved pasta water, a little at a time, to create a light sauce. Toss gently.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Grate fresh Parmesan cheese over each portion if desired.
notes: Bresaola is a cured, air-dried beef. Its delicate flavor is best preserved by adding it at the end of cooking.
Adjust the amount of pasta water to achieve desired sauce consistency.
traditional_techniques: Aglio e olio base for flavor

recipes.recipe_name: Peruvian Lomo Saltado
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lomo Saltado is presented on a clean white porcelain plate. The dish features 3cm seared beef tenderloin cubes with a dark, glossy crust. Thick-cut red onion wedges and bright red tomato wedges are tossed with yellow bell pepper batons, showing vibrant colors and slight char marks. The ingredients are arranged in a natural, mounded pile, coated in a shimmering dark brown sauce. Golden-brown potato batons are interspersed throughout the beef and vegetables. A neat mound of fluffy white rice sits adjacent to the stir-fry. The scene is set on a rustic wooden bistro table with a linen napkin and a small bowl of green chili sauce. Natural light highlights the textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with Aji Verde (spicy green chili sauce)
Accompany with Inca Kola or a Pisco Sour
Traditionally eaten using a fork and spoon
instructions: Peel potatoes and cut into 1cm batons.
Soak batons in cold water for 20 minutes.
Drain and dry potatoes completely with a towel.
Heat oil to 180°C in a heavy pot.
Fry potatoes until golden and crisp. Drain on paper.
Season potatoes with salt immediately.
Boil rice in 450ml salted water until tender. Keep warm.
Season beef cubes with salt and pepper.
Heat a wok over high heat with 15ml oil until smoking.
Sear beef cubes in batches until heavily browned. Remove.
Add onions and peppers to the wok. Sáuté for 2 minutes.
Add garlic. Stir for 30 seconds.
Return beef to the wok. Add tomato wedges.
Pour in tamari and vinegar. Toss for 1 minute over high heat.
Fold in cilantro and fried potatoes. Serve immediately with rice.
notes: Ensure the wok is smoking hot for authentic flavor
Remove tomato seeds to prevent the sauce from becoming watery
Use Tamari specifically to maintain the gluten-free requirement

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Lemon Herb Chicken with Potatoes and Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of roasted lemon herb chicken, potatoes, and mushrooms rests on a simple, cream-colored ceramic plate with a slightly uneven, handmade texture. Two golden-brown roasted chicken thighs, with crispy skin and visible herbs, are placed centrally. Around them, thick-cut roasted potato wedges, tender roasted cremini mushroom halves, and caramelized red onion wedges are naturally arranged, some overlapping, creating a comforting mound. A few charred lemon slices are tucked among the vegetables. The dish is garnished simply with a scattering of fresh chopped parsley and a small sprig of fresh rosemary. The natural colors are warm and inviting: rich browns, golden yellows, and earthy greens. The plate is positioned on a well-used, dark wooden dining table, showing natural grain and minor imperfections. A casual, folded linen napkin in a neutral tone and a simple metal fork and knife are placed beside the plate. The scene is lit with warm, soft light, mimicking a cozy evening in a family kitchen, with a slight blur in the background to keep focus on the food.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and scrub potatoes. Cut potatoes into thick-cut wedges.
Wipe mushrooms clean. Halve larger mushrooms. Leave smaller ones whole.
Peel red onion. Cut into thick wedges.
Mince garlic cloves.
Remove rosemary and thyme leaves from stems. Chop roughly.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. This ensures crispy skin.
In a large bowl, combine chicken, potato wedges, mushroom halves, and onion wedges.
Add olive oil, minced garlic, chopped rosemary, chopped thyme, salt, and black pepper. Toss well to coat all ingredients evenly.
Slice half of the lemon into thin rounds. Add to the bowl. Squeeze juice from the other half over the mixture.
Spread ingredients in a single layer on a large baking sheet or roasting pan. Do not overcrowd.
Roast for 35-45 minutes. Chicken should reach an internal temperature of 75°C. Vegetables should be tender and lightly browned.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.
For extra crispy potatoes, soak wedges in cold water for 30 minutes then pat very dry before tossing with oil.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast with Lemon-Herb Butter Sauce
recipes.visual_description: The pan-seared chicken breast, cooked to a rich golden-brown, rests as a substantial, whole piece or two thick, diagonal chunks on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Its exterior shows a slight crispness, while the interior is visibly tender. Alongside, a vibrant green cluster of roasted asparagus spears, slightly charred at the tips, adds a contrasting color and texture. A luscious, pale yellow lemon-herb butter sauce, flecked with bright green chopped parsley and thyme, is generously spooned over the chicken, glistening under the light. A fresh sprig of parsley or thyme garnishes the dish, with a bright lemon wedge placed beside it. The overall presentation is professional and approachable, with moderate negative space. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by standard silverware and a folded cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting in a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with standard European flatware.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat.

Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer pan to a preheated oven at 190°C. Cook 8-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken. Rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.
While chicken rests, add 30g butter to the same pan over medium heat. Sauté minced shallot 2 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Reduce liquid by half.
Add chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce liquid by half again.
Remove pan from heat. Whisk in remaining 30g butter until melted and sauce emulsifies. Stir in lemon juice, chopped parsley, and chopped thyme.
Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Meanwhile, toss asparagus spears with remaining 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast at 190°C for 8-10 minutes until tender-crisp.

Slice each chicken breast into two thick diagonal chunks, or serve whole. Arrange chicken on individual plates with roasted asparagus spears beside it. Spoon lemon-herb butter sauce generously over the chicken.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature for food safety.
Resting the chicken after cooking is crucial for juiciness.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Potato and Mushroom Bake
recipes.visual_description: A hearty individual portion of Rustic Potato and Mushroom Bake rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The dish features golden-brown roasted potato cubes, earthy quartered cremini mushrooms, vibrant red, green, and yellow bell pepper squares, and caramelized thin onion slices. Ingredients are naturally mounded, showcasing varied textures: crisp potato edges, tender interiors, and soft, browned vegetables. A few fresh thyme sprigs garnish the top. The plate sits on a simple wooden table within a modern bistro setting. A neatly folded cotton napkin and standard silver flatware are positioned beside the plate. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting colors and inviting textures. The background is softly blurred, maintaining focus on the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with a side of crusty artisan bread and a simple green salad with vinaigrette.

ingredients.name: Potatoes (e.g., Maris Piper or Yukon Gold)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
In a large bowl, combine cubed potatoes, quartered mushrooms, bell pepper squares, and sliced onions.
Add minced garlic, olive oil, thyme sprigs, rosemary sprigs, salt, and black pepper. Toss well to coat all vegetables.
Transfer mixture to a large baking dish (approx. 30x20 cm). Spread in an even layer.
Pour vegetable broth over the vegetables.
Bake for 30 minutes.
Stir vegetables gently. If using, sprinkle grated Parmesan cheese over the top.
Return to oven. Bake for another 25-35 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and top is golden brown.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Gnocchi with Spicy Cannellini Bean Ragu
recipes.visual_description: This dish features tender potato gnocchi coated in a vibrant, rustic ragu, served in a classic white porcelain bowl. The ragu presents a rich red hue from the crushed tomatoes, studded with creamy white cannellini beans and tiny flecks of red chili. Finely diced onion and minced garlic are visibly integrated within the sauce, which clings beautifully to the soft, pillowy gnocchi. Fresh, vibrant green basil leaves are torn and scattered generously over the top, providing a striking color contrast and aromatic freshness. A subtle sheen of olive oil indicates the sauce's richness. The overall presentation is inviting and generous, with moderate negative space on the plate. A simple wooden table and a folded cotton napkin complete the casual bistro setting, with natural, even lighting highlighting the dish's comforting appeal. A fork and spoon rest beside the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta bread to soak up the sauce.
Offer a simple green salad with a light vinaigrette as an accompaniment.
Pair with a medium-bodied Italian red wine, such as Chianti.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and red chili flakes. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer.
Add drained cannellini beans. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
While ragu simmers, cook gnocchi according to package directions. Gnocchi are ready when they float to the surface.
Drain gnocchi. Add cooked gnocchi directly to the ragu.
Toss gently to coat. Remove from heat.
Stir in half of the fresh basil leaves, torn. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with remaining fresh basil and grated Parmesan cheese, if using.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tomato Chicken Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Tomato Chicken Pasta is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple wooden table. The penne pasta is coated in a luscious, creamy reddish-orange tomato sauce, forming a gently mounded pile. Nestled within and atop the pasta are several golden-brown, seared chicken medallions, cut into thick, substantial chunks, showcasing their tender interior. The dish is garnished with vibrant green chopped fresh parsley, providing a fresh contrast. The overall presentation is clean and professional, with moderate negative space around the food. A standard silver fork and knife rest beside the plate on a white cotton napkin. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, creating a casual yet refined bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with standard flatware.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside. Let rest 5 minutes.
Cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 100 ml pasta water.
Dice onion. Mince garlic. Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the same skillet. Sauté diced onion 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in heavy cream and American cheese slices until cheese is fully melted and sauce is smooth.
Add cooked pasta to the sauce. Toss to coat evenly. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water gradually until desired consistency is reached.
Slice rested chicken breasts into thick medallions or substantial chunks.
Serve pasta onto plates. Arrange chicken medallions on top of the pasta. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Egg Custard with Roasted Cherry Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of savory egg custard is presented in a pristine white porcelain ramekin, placed on a simple round white dinner plate. The custard has a delicate golden-yellow hue, slightly puffed at the edges, indicating a creamy, tender texture. Embedded within the custard are vibrant red, roasted cherry tomatoes, some visibly burst, adding pockets of bright color and soft texture. A sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped green chives and parsley garnishes the top, providing a subtle color contrast and fresh aroma. The ramekin sits on a clean, light-colored wooden table surface, suggesting a modern bistro setting. A neatly folded cotton napkin and standard silver flatware are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its warmth and simple elegance. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space, creating a professional yet approachable presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with slices of crusty baguette.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with a light vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Place cherry tomatoes on a baking tray. Drizzle with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 15-20 minutes until softened and slightly burst.
Finely dice the shallot. Mince the garlic.

Heat butter and remaining olive oil in a small pan over medium heat. Add diced shallot and sauté until translucent, about 3 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Remove from heat.
In a large bowl, whisk eggs, milk, chopped chives, and chopped parsley. Season with salt and pepper.
Stir in the grated cheese and sautéed shallot-garlic mixture.
Lightly grease four 150 ml ramekins. Divide the roasted cherry tomatoes among the ramekins.
Carefully pour the egg mixture over the tomatoes in each ramekin.
Place ramekins in a baking dish. Pour hot water into the baking dish to come halfway up the sides of the ramekins (bain-marie).
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until custards are set but still slightly wobbly in the center. Do not overcook.
Remove ramekins from water bath. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Do not overbake the custards; they should be just set and creamy, not rubbery.
Ensure the water for the bain-marie is hot to help even cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Spicy Strawberry-Apple Relish
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant pan-seared chicken breast anchors the center of a clean white porcelain dinner plate, presented as a whole, succulent piece. The chicken exhibits a golden-brown, lightly caramelized crust, indicating a perfect sear. Adjacent to it, a rich, glossy spicy strawberry-apple relish with softened fruit chunks adds a pop of reddish-orange, contrasting beautifully with the chicken. Roasted cherry tomatoes, their skins slightly blistered and deepened in color, are artfully scattered alongside, interspersed with dark, halved Kalamata olives and soft, roasted garlic cloves. Crisp, golden-brown rustic bread croutons, cut into irregular 2cm cubes, are sprinkled over the dish, providing textural contrast. A light dusting of fresh, bright green chopped parsley adds a final touch of color and freshness. The plate is presented on a simple wooden table, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting in a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). Toss cherry tomatoes and 2 whole garlic cloves with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes until softened and slightly charred.

Dice apple into 1cm cubes. Hull and quarter strawberries. In a small saucepan, combine diced apple, quartered strawberries, minced garlic, brown sugar, and hot sauce. Cook over medium heat for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until fruit softens and mixture thickens slightly.

Cube rustic bread into 2cm pieces. In a large pan, melt 15g butter with 15ml olive oil over medium heat. Add bread cubes. Toast, stirring frequently, until golden brown and crisp on all sides. Remove from pan and set aside.
In the same pan, melt remaining 15g butter over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Sear for 6-8 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Roughly chop roasted garlic cloves. Pit and halve Kalamata olives. Combine roasted tomatoes, chopped roasted garlic, and halved olives.

Place one seared chicken breast on each plate. Spoon a generous amount of the spicy strawberry-apple relish alongside. Arrange the roasted tomato-olive mixture next to the chicken. Scatter garlic croutons over and around the dish. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Carrot and Apple Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spiced Carrot and Apple Crumble is presented in a deep, off-white ceramic bowl, placed on a well-used wooden kitchen table. The crumble topping is golden brown, rustic, and slightly uneven, with some larger clumps and visible oats, hinting at its homemade origin. Patches of the warm, amber-toned apple and grated carrot filling peek through the cracks in the crust, showing its soft, bubbling texture. A generous dollop of thick, white cream rests on top or beside the crumble. The setting is a homely family kitchen, with warm, natural lighting. A simple, silver spoon rests beside the bowl on a casually placed cloth napkin. The overall impression is one of comforting, unpretentious warmth, inviting immediate enjoyment.

ingredients.name: Apples (e.g., Bramley or Granny Smith), peeled, cored, diced into 2 cm cubes

instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (fan 160°C).
Combine diced apples, grated carrots, granulated sugar, 30g brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, lemon juice, and cornflour in a large bowl. Mix well.
Spoon fruit mixture into a 1.5-liter baking dish.
For the crumble, place flour and cold butter in a separate bowl. Rub butter into flour with fingertips until mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs.
Stir in oats, 70g brown sugar, and salt. Mix until just combined.
Sprinkle crumble topping evenly over the fruit mixture.
Bake for 30-40 minutes, or until topping is golden brown and fruit filling is bubbling.
notes: Serve warm with a dollop of thick cream, vanilla ice cream, or custard.

recipes.recipe_name: Crespelle di Robiola e Spinaci
recipes.visual_description: Two golden-brown crespelle are arranged on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, gently overlapping. Each crespella is filled with vibrant green spinach and creamy white robiola cheese, with a hint of the filling peeking from the folds. A smooth, pale cream sauce coats the crespelle, glistening under natural, even lighting. The dish is garnished with a scattering of freshly chopped bright green parsley, providing a fresh contrast. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space on the plate. The plate sits on a simple wooden surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin, evoking a relaxed yet refined modern bistro setting, highlighting the dish as the centerpiece.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with extra grated Parmesan cheese.
Accompany with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
instructions: Sift flour into a large bowl. Create a well in the center.
Crack eggs into the well. Whisk eggs gradually, incorporating flour.
Slowly add milk, whisking constantly until batter is smooth. Add a pinch of salt. Let batter rest 30 minutes.
Wash spinach thoroughly. Wilt spinach in a hot pan without oil until softened. Drain excess water, squeeze dry, and finely chop.
In a bowl, combine chopped spinach, robiola cheese, 25 g grated Parmesan, and a pinch of nutmeg. Mix well. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat a lightly buttered 20 cm non-stick pan over medium heat. Pour a small ladle of batter, tilting to coat the bottom evenly. Cook 1-2 minutes until edges are golden. Flip and cook 30 seconds more. Transfer crespelle to a plate. Repeat with remaining batter to make 8 crespelle.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease a baking dish.

Place a spoonful of spinach-robiola filling on one half of each crespella. Fold in half, then fold again to create a quarter-circle or roll into a cylinder. Arrange filled crespelle in the prepared baking dish.
In a small saucepan, melt 20 g butter. Stir in cream and remaining 25 g Parmesan. Heat gently until sauce is warm and smooth. Do not boil. Season with salt and pepper.
Pour cream sauce evenly over the crespelle in the baking dish. Bake 15-20 minutes, or until bubbling and lightly golden on top.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: One-Pan Lemon Herb Roasted Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of One-Pan Lemon Herb Roasted Chicken and Potatoes is presented on a simple, round ceramic plate with a subtle, natural glaze. The plate, perhaps in an off-white or light grey, sits on a well-worn wooden dining table. The centerpiece is a golden-brown roasted chicken thigh, its skin crispy and slightly darkened from the oven. Alongside it are several rustic potato wedges, their edges crisped and interiors tender, showing some of the potato skin. Scattered amongst the chicken and potatoes are softened, caramelized lemon slices and a few fragrant sprigs of roasted rosemary and thyme. The arrangement is natural and casual, with components touching and slightly overlapping, reflecting a homely, comforting meal. The lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a cozy kitchen. A simple cloth napkin and a standard fork and knife are casually placed beside the plate. The overall scene is unfussy, highlighting the expertly cooked, hearty comfort food.

ingredients.name: Small potatoes (e.g., Yukon Gold or new potatoes)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels.
Cut potatoes into 2-3 cm wedges. Do not peel.
Slice lemon into thin rounds.
Smash garlic cloves with the side of a knife.
In a large bowl, combine chicken, potato wedges, olive oil, salt, and pepper. Toss well to coat.
Add lemon slices, smashed garlic, rosemary sprigs, and thyme sprigs to the bowl. Toss gently to distribute.
Spread the chicken and potato mixture in a single layer on a large baking sheet. Do not overcrowd the pan.
Roast for 40-50 minutes, or until chicken is golden brown and cooked through.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F) with a meat thermometer.
Serve immediately directly from the baking sheet or transfer to a large platter.
notes: This recipe offers minimal cleanup, making it perfect for weeknight dinners.
Ensure chicken reaches a safe internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).

recipes.recipe_name: Zero-Waste Corn & Kudzu Fritters
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of three to four golden-brown, irregularly shaped corn and kudzu fritters is artfully arranged on a round, handcrafted ceramic plate in a warm off-white tone. The fritters are cooked to a delicate crisp exterior, revealing the natural textures of the corn kernels within. A generous dollop of creamy, off-white fermented sour cream sits beside the fritters. A vibrant, deep orange-red annatto glaze is artfully drizzled over the fritters and lightly around the plate, creating striking visual lines. The plating is minimalistic, with ample negative space highlighting the natural beauty of each component. A few fresh, bright green cilantro leaves are scattered thoughtfully as a garnish. The entire setup rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by a natural undyed linen napkin. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish, emphasizing its earthy colors and textures. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of natural greenery visible, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.
instructions: Prepare fermented sour cream: Combine sour cream with 5 ml white vinegar. Cover loosely. Let stand at room temperature for 12-24 hours until slightly tangy. Refrigerate.
Shuck corn. Cut kernels from cobs. Reserve cobs.
Make corn cob stock: Place reserved corn cobs in a saucepan. Add 500 ml water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer for 20 minutes. Strain stock. Discard cobs.
Finely dice red onion. Mince garlic. Chop cilantro.
Combine corn kernels, diced onion, minced garlic, and chopped cilantro in a large bowl.
Dissolve kudzu starch in 50 ml of the warm corn cob stock. Stir until smooth. Add to corn mixture.
Season corn mixture with salt and pepper. Mix well to form a thick batter.
Heat 30 ml vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat.
Spoon 2-3 tablespoons of batter per fritter into the hot pan. Flatten slightly. Do not overcrowd.
Cook fritters for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Repeat with remaining batter. Add more oil as needed. Keep warm.

Prepare annatto glaze: Heat remaining 20 ml vegetable oil in a small saucepan over low heat. Add annatto seeds. Cook gently for 2-3 minutes until oil turns deep orange-red. Do not burn seeds. Strain oil. Discard seeds.
Return annatto oil to the saucepan. Add lime cordial, apricot liqueur, and eau de vie. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 2 minutes until slightly reduced and syrupy. Season with a pinch of salt.
To serve, arrange 3-4 fritters on each plate. Dollop a spoonful of fermented sour cream next to the fritters. Drizzle generously with the annatto glaze.
Garnish with a few fresh cilantro leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Mushroom Potato Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A hearty, rustic individual portion of Chicken and Mushroom Potato Skillet is presented in a deep, slightly chipped ceramic bowl, showcasing the comforting essence of Russian home cooking. Generous chunks of seared chicken, tender 2-3cm potato cubes, quartered mushrooms, diced carrots, and diced red bell pepper are coated in a rich, simmering tomato-based sauce. The sauce, a warm reddish-brown, envelops the ingredients, highlighting their natural colors. A dollop of creamy white smetana (sour cream) rests atop the stew, partially melting into the sauce, and a generous sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped dill and parsley adds a bright counterpoint. The dish is set on a well-used wooden dining table, alongside a thick slice of dark rye bread. A simple, folded linen napkin and a sturdy metal spoon complete the authentic, lived-in family kitchen scene, bathed in warm, natural light.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a generous dollop of smetana (sour cream) on top.
Accompany with slices of dark rye bread for dipping into the sauce.
Traditionally served with pickled vegetables (e.g., pickled cucumbers or tomatoes) on the side.
instructions: Pat chicken chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pan. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrot, and red bell pepper to the same pan. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Stir in minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add quartered mushrooms and cook for 5-7 minutes until they release their liquid and start to brown.
Sprinkle flour over the vegetables and stir for 1 minute to cook out raw flour taste.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Add bay leaf. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Return seared chicken to the pan. Add cubed potatoes. Stir to combine.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (75°C internal temperature) and potatoes are tender. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve hot, topped with a dollop of sour cream (smetana) and a generous sprinkle of fresh chopped dill and parsley.
notes: The consistency of the stew can be adjusted by adding a little more broth if a thinner sauce is desired.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
traditional_techniques: Zazharka (sautéing vegetables to create a flavorful base)

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Pasta Carbonara with Cured Egg Yolk
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Sustainable Pasta Carbonara rests on a cream-colored, handcrafted ceramic plate. The spaghetti is twirled into a natural, unforced mound, glistening with a creamy, pale yellow emulsified sauce. Specks of freshly cracked black pepper are visible throughout the pasta. A generous, vibrant orange dusting of finely grated cured egg yolk crowns the dish, providing a striking color contrast and emphasizing the preservation technique. The plate is positioned on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by simple, elegant Italian flatware (a fork and spoon). A natural, undyed linen napkin is subtly placed to the side. The background is minimalist and clean, with soft, diffused natural lighting illuminating the dish, highlighting its organic textures and colors. The entire plate is visible, showcasing mindful negative space and a clean composition.
instructions: Prepare cured egg yolks at least 4 days in advance: Combine 1 cup salt and 1 cup sugar. Bury egg yolks in mixture. Cure in refrigerator 4-7 days until firm. Rinse yolks and pat dry.

Prepare fermented garlic at least 1 week in advance: Place peeled garlic cloves in a clean jar. Cover with a 2% salt brine (2g salt per 100ml water). Seal jar. Ferment at room temperature 1-2 weeks until bubbly and tangy. Refrigerate.
Make zero-waste vegetable broth: Simmer vegetable scraps (onion peels, carrot ends, celery tops, mushroom stems) in water for 30 minutes. Strain.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente.
While pasta cooks, prepare sauce base. In a medium bowl, whisk fresh egg yolks, grated Pecorino Romano, and black pepper until smooth. Set aside.
In a large skillet over medium heat, add olive oil. Sauté minced fermented garlic for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Drain pasta, reserving 250 ml of pasta cooking water.
Add cooked pasta to the skillet with garlic. Toss to coat.
Gradually add 120 ml reserved pasta water and 100 ml vegetable broth to the egg yolk mixture, whisking constantly to temper the eggs. This creates a smooth, creamy emulsion.

Pour egg mixture over pasta in the skillet. Toss quickly and continuously over low heat for 1-2 minutes until sauce thickens and coats pasta. Do not scramble eggs. Add more pasta water if needed for desired consistency.
Taste and adjust salt if necessary. The cheese and cured yolks add saltiness.
Serve immediately. Grate cured egg yolks generously over each portion.

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Basil Chicken with Jasmine Rice
recipes.visual_description: A steaming mound of fluffy jasmine rice occupies half of a clean white porcelain plate. Beside it, glossy 2cm chunks of golden-brown seared chicken thighs are coated in a dark, savory sauce. Vibrant green Thai basil leaves are wilted throughout the stir-fry. A single fried egg with a lacy, golden-crisp edge and a bright runny yolk rests atop the chicken. The dish is presented on a dark teak wood table with a small side dish of fish sauce containing sliced red chilies. Soft natural lighting highlights the textures of the crispy egg and tender chicken. A traditional Thai stainless steel spoon and fork lie on a white cotton napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with Prik Nam Pla (fish sauce with chilies)
Eat with a spoon in the right hand and fork in the left
Provide cucumber slices to cool the palate
instructions: Rinse rice until water runs clear.
Cook rice in 600ml water until fluffy.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan over high heat.
Fry eggs until edges are crispy and brown.
Remove eggs and set aside.
Heat remaining oil in a wok.
Sauté garlic and chilies until fragrant.
Add chicken chunks to the wok.
Stir-fry chicken until browned and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Stir in oyster sauce, soy sauces, and sugar.
Add basil leaves and toss until wilted.
Divide rice into four plates.
Top rice with chicken and a fried egg.
notes: Use Holy Basil for the most authentic flavor if available.
Adjust chili count based on heat preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato and Caramelized Onion Salad
recipes.visual_description: A generous portion of creamy Potato and Caramelized Onion Salad is mounded casually in a rustic, off-white ceramic bowl, typical of a well-loved home kitchen. Diced, tender Yukon Gold potatoes, their natural yellow hues visible, are gently mixed with thinly sliced, golden-brown caramelized onions, creating a comforting blend of textures. A rich, creamy whole grain mustard dressing coats every component, ensuring full flavor integration. The salad is garnished simply with a scattering of fresh, chopped green parsley and a few crispy bacon bits for added savory depth and texture, maintaining a homely, unpretentious appearance. The bowl sits on a worn wooden dining table, alongside a simple fork and a casually folded cloth napkin. Warm, inviting light from a kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, capturing the essence of a relaxed family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a side dish for barbecues, picnics, or family dinners.
Often accompanied by grilled meats or sandwiches.
instructions: Wash potatoes. Boil whole potatoes in salted water until fork-tender, about 20-25 minutes. Drain and let cool slightly. Dice cooled potatoes into 2 cm cubes.
Peel and thinly slice onions. In a large skillet, cook sliced onions over medium-low heat with a little oil until deeply golden and caramelized, about 20-25 minutes. Stir occasionally.
While onions cook, crisp bacon in a separate pan if using. Drain on paper towels. Crumble into small bits.
In a large bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, whole grain mustard, apple cider vinegar, salt, and black pepper until smooth.
Add diced potatoes and caramelized onions to the dressing. Gently fold until all ingredients are evenly coated.
Stir in chopped fresh parsley.
Serve the salad warm or chilled. Garnish with crumbled bacon bits, if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef with Fermented Onion Relish and Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Braised Beef with Fermented Onion Relish and Root Vegetables is presented on a round, handcrafted ceramic plate in a creamy beige tone. A substantial, naturally shaped chunk of deeply browned, tender braised beef sits as the focal point. Beside it, two or three large, rustic chunks of roasted root vegetables – vibrant orange carrots, pale parsnips, and light brown potato halves – are casually arranged, their charred edges adding visual interest. A spoonful of translucent, pale pink fermented red onion relish is placed on the beef or beside it, providing a pop of color and contrasting texture. A fresh sprig of parsley or thyme garnishes the dish. The plating is clean and unforced, celebrating natural ingredient beauty. The setting features an eco-conscious light wood table, with an undyed linen napkin. Soft, natural lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting earthy colors and textures. The background is minimalist, with a hint of natural greenery for an organic feel.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Onion Relish (5-7 days in advance): Dissolve 1 tbsp sea salt in 500ml filtered water to make brine. Pack thinly sliced red onions tightly into a clean glass jar. Pour brine over onions, ensuring they are fully submerged. Use a fermentation weight or small clean jar to keep onions under liquid. Seal jar loosely or use an airlock lid. Ferment at room temperature (18-24°C) for 5-7 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Refrigerate once fermented.

Sear Beef: Pat beef chunks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef from pot.
Sauté Aromatics: Add coarsely chopped brown onions to the pot. Sauté until softened and lightly caramelized, about 8-10 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Deglaze and Braise: Pour in red wine (if using). Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Reduce wine by half. Return beef to the pot. Pour in beef stock. Add rosemary and thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover tightly. Braise in the oven at 160°C (325°F) for 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).

Prepare Root Vegetables: Toss carrots, parsnips, and potatoes with 1 tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast in a separate oven at 200°C (390°F) for 30-40 minutes, or until tender and lightly browned.

Serve: Place one large braised beef chunk on each plate. Arrange roasted root vegetable chunks alongside. Spoon a generous portion of the Fermented Onion Relish over or next to the beef. Garnish with a fresh sprig of parsley or thyme.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by encouraging homemade beef stock from bones/trimmings. Vegetable scraps from root vegetables and onion skins can be saved for future vegetable stocks.
Fermentation of onions is a key preservation technique used in this sustainable dish.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken, Fermented Potato Purée, Zero-Waste Pesto
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken thigh, with its crispy, golden-brown skin, rests on a handcrafted, cream-colored ceramic plate. The chicken is whole, presenting a succulent, rustic appearance. Beside it, a generous, organic dollop of creamy, off-white fermented potato purée displays natural swirls, suggesting a soft, airy texture. Leaning against the chicken or purée is a delicate, irregular golden-brown cheese tuile, its intricate texture adding a subtle crisp element. Vibrant green zero-waste pesto is artfully drizzled in a few drops around the plate, providing a fresh color contrast. The plating emphasizes negative space, allowing each component to stand out. The scene is set on a light-colored, reclaimed wood table, complemented by an undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the dish from the side, enhancing its textures and colors. A minimalist background features blurred green foliage, hinting at natural elements and an eco-conscious setting. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a refined, restaurant-style portion.

ingredients.name: Carrot tops or herb stems (e.g., parsley, basil)

instructions: Prepare fermented potato liquid: Combine 250 ml filtered water with 5 g salt. Peel potatoes; reserve peels. Submerge potato peels in salted water. Cover loosely. Ferment at room temperature 3-5 days. Strain liquid; discard peels. Reserve liquid for purée.
Trim excess fat from chicken thighs; reserve trimmings and bones for stock. Pat chicken dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Make zero-waste pesto: Wash carrot tops or herb stems thoroughly. In a food processor, combine carrot tops/herb stems, sunflower seeds, 1 garlic clove, 50 ml olive oil, and juice from half a lemon. Process until smooth. Season with salt.

Make cheese tuiles: Grate hard cheese finely. Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat. Sprinkle small mounds of grated cheese onto the hot pan, leaving space between. Cook 2-3 minutes until golden and crispy. Transfer to a wire rack to cool and harden. Break into irregular pieces.

Prepare potatoes: Peel potatoes. Cut into uniform 3 cm cubes. Place in a pot. Cover with cold water. Add a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat; simmer 15-20 minutes until fork-tender. Drain well.

Make fermented potato purée: Return drained potatoes to the pot. Add milk, butter, remaining garlic clove (minced), and 50 ml of the fermented potato liquid. Mash until smooth. Add more fermented liquid or milk to achieve desired creamy consistency. Season with salt and pepper.

Sear chicken thighs: Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down. Sear 8-10 minutes until skin is golden and crispy. Flip chicken. Transfer pan to a preheated oven at 190°C (375°F). Roast 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Rest chicken 5 minutes.

Plate: Place a generous dollop of fermented potato purée on one side of a handcrafted ceramic plate. Place one seared chicken thigh beside the purée. Arrange 1-2 crispy cheese tuile pieces against the chicken or purée. Drizzle zero-waste pesto around the dish. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pasta with Fermented Tomato & Braised Greens
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pasta is presented in a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic bowl. The pasta, such as rigatoni or paccheri, is coated in a vibrant, rustic red fermented tomato sauce. Deep green, tender braised cavolo nero leaves are scattered throughout the pasta, providing color and textural contrast. A few fresh basil leaves are placed naturally on top. The pasta has a slight sheen, the greens appear tender and slightly wilted, and the sauce shows subtle texture from the mashed tomatoes. The bowl rests on a light, naturally textured reclaimed wood table surface. A simple, undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is folded beside the bowl. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish from the side, creating gentle shadows. The background is clean and minimalist, possibly with a hint of a blurred green plant.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately as a primo piatto.
Offer crusty bread to soak up extra sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad.

ingredients.name: Seasonal Greens (e.g., Cavolo Nero, Swiss Chard)

instructions: Prepare fermented tomatoes: Roughly chop 1 kg overripe tomatoes. Place in a clean jar with 20g sea salt. Cover loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 5-7 days, burping daily, until tangy.
Strain fermented tomatoes, reserving fermentation liquid. Roughly chop fermented tomatoes.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add 2 cloves minced garlic and 2g chilli flakes. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chopped fermented tomatoes to the pan. Cook 10 minutes, mashing with a spoon. Add 100ml reserved fermentation liquid. Simmer 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook 400g pasta according to package directions in salted water until al dente. Reserve 150ml pasta cooking water.
While pasta cooks, wash and roughly chop 200g seasonal greens.
In a separate pan, heat 15ml olive oil. Add chopped greens. Sauté until wilted. Add 100ml vegetable broth. Braise 5-7 minutes until tender. Season with salt and pepper.
Drain pasta. Add pasta to the tomato sauce. Add 50-100ml pasta cooking water as needed to create a light sauce. Toss to combine.
Divide pasta among serving plates. Top each portion with braised greens. Garnish with fresh basil or oregano.
notes: Fermentation time for tomatoes can vary based on temperature. Taste daily for desired tang.
Use any seasonal greens available, such as spinach, chard, or even broccoli rabe.
Vegetable broth can be made from saved vegetable scraps (e.g., carrot peels, onion skins, celery ends) simmered with water for a zero-waste approach.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Chicken Arrabbiata Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of Spicy Chicken Arrabbiata Pasta is presented centrally on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Al dente penne pasta, coated in a vibrant, glossy, deep red tomato sauce, is piled neatly. Seared chicken chunks, golden-brown and tender, are interspersed throughout the pasta, showcasing their irregular, rustic shapes. The sauce has visible flecks of red chili and thinly sliced garlic. A generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped fresh parsley provides a striking color contrast and freshness. The dish is framed by a moderate amount of negative space on the plate. The setting features a simple wooden table surface with a subtle grain. A standard silver fork and spoon are placed to the right of the plate, and a folded cotton napkin rests to the left. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the textures. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping into the sauce.
Offer grated Pecorino Romano or Parmesan cheese on the side.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Cut chicken breast into 3cm thick chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add remaining 30ml olive oil to the same pan. Add finely diced red onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add thinly sliced garlic and red chili flakes. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not burn garlic.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly.
While sauce simmers, cook penne pasta in a large pot of salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta, reserving 120ml pasta water.
Return cooked chicken to the sauce. Add drained pasta and half of the chopped fresh parsley to the pan.
Toss pasta with sauce and chicken to combine. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, 30ml at a time, until desired consistency is reached.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley and grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: Adjust the amount of red chili flakes to suit your preferred spice level. For less heat, remove seeds from fresh chilies.

recipes.recipe_name: Carrot and Apple Tarte Tatin
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of golden-brown Carrot and Apple Tarte Tatin rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The tarte is round, featuring deeply caramelized apple wedges and carrot batons arranged in a spiral pattern, showcasing their rich, glossy texture. The puff pastry crust, flaky and golden, forms a crisp base. A small, elegant dollop of bright white crème fraîche is placed beside the tarte, offering a visual contrast. The plate has moderate negative space, enhancing the tarte's prominence. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table surface and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dessert's warmth and inviting colors. The presentation is professional yet approachable, reflecting classic French simplicity.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm with a dollop of crème fraîche.
Can also be served with vanilla bean ice cream.

ingredients.name: Crème fraîche or vanilla bean ice cream (for serving)

instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (fan assisted).
Peel, core, and cut apples into 8 thick wedges each.
Peel carrots. Cut into 5cm long, 1cm thick batons.
In a 20cm oven-safe, heavy-bottomed skillet, melt butter over medium heat.
Add sugar and pinch of salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, until a golden amber caramel forms. Do not burn.
Remove skillet from heat. Carefully arrange apple wedges and carrot batons in a concentric pattern in the caramel, packing them tightly.
Sprinkle with ground cinnamon and lemon juice.
Unroll puff pastry. Cut a circle slightly larger than the skillet diameter.
Place pastry over fruit, gently tucking the edges down around the fruit inside the skillet.
Cut a small vent in the center of the pastry to allow steam to escape.
Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until the pastry is golden brown and puffed.
Remove from oven. Let the tarte cool in the skillet for 5 minutes.
Place a large serving plate over the skillet. Carefully and confidently invert the tarte onto the plate.
Serve warm with a dollop of crème fraîche or a scoop of vanilla bean ice cream.
notes: Ensure the caramel reaches a deep amber color for best flavor, but be careful not to burn it.
The apples and carrots should be packed tightly in the skillet to create a cohesive tarte.

recipes.recipe_name: Amaranth-Crusted Chicken with Aji Amarillo Sauce and Andean Quinoa Salad
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared amaranth-crusted chicken breast is the focal point, cut into thick diagonal slices revealing its tender interior and golden-brown, crispy exterior. The chicken is arranged neatly on a clean white porcelain plate, with a rich, vibrant yellow aji amarillo sauce generously drizzled over and beside it. Adjacent is a vibrant mound of Andean quinoa salad, featuring fluffy quinoa mixed with small diced red bell pepper, green cucumber, and halved red cherry tomatoes, brightened by fresh cilantro. The plating is professional and balanced, with moderate negative space. The dish rests on a simple wooden table surface with a cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors against a soft, casual restaurant-style background. Subtle blurred Peruvian textiles hint at cultural origin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra aji amarillo sauce on the side for dipping.
Can be accompanied by a small portion of simple white rice or roasted potatoes.
Offer a small side of rocoto chili paste for those desiring more heat.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Set up a dredging station: one plate with plain wheat flour, one shallow bowl with beaten eggs, one plate with amaranth flour.
Dredge each chicken breast first in plain flour, shaking off excess. Dip in egg, letting excess drip off. Coat thoroughly with amaranth flour, pressing to adhere.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Carefully place chicken breasts in hot oil. Do not overcrowd. Pan-fry for 5-7 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Remove chicken from skillet. Place on a wire rack to drain excess oil. Keep warm.
For Aji Amarillo Sauce: In a small saucepan, sauté diced red onion in a teaspoon of oil until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute.
Stir in aji amarillo paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in evaporated milk. Bring to a gentle simmer. Add crumbled queso fresco or feta. Stir until cheese melts and sauce thickens slightly.
Season sauce with salt to taste. Remove from heat. Keep warm.
For Quinoa Salad: In a large bowl, combine cooked quinoa, diced cucumber, halved cherry tomatoes, diced red bell pepper, and chopped cilantro.
In a small bowl, whisk together lime juice and olive oil. Season with salt and pepper.
Pour dressing over quinoa mixture. Toss gently to combine.
To serve, slice each chicken breast diagonally into 3-4 thick pieces. Arrange on individual plates.
Spoon a generous amount of Aji Amarillo sauce over and beside the chicken. Serve a portion of Andean Quinoa Salad alongside.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked to 75°C (167°F) internal temperature for safety.
Aji amarillo paste is available in Latin American markets or online. Its unique fruity heat is essential to Peruvian cuisine.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Chicken and Brown Rice Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean Chicken and Brown Rice Skillet is presented on a clean white porcelain plate, centrally placed on a simple wooden table. One golden-brown seared chicken thigh sits atop a bed of fluffy, earthy brown rice. Scattered around the chicken are vibrant halved cherry tomatoes and dark Kalamata olives, adding pops of red and black. The dish is garnished with bright green chopped fresh parsley and creamy white crumbled feta cheese. A lemon wedge is placed beside the chicken. The textures are varied: crisp chicken skin, tender rice, juicy tomatoes. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish. A folded white cotton napkin and standard flatware rest beside the plate. A warm pita bread is subtly placed on the side, inviting cultural accompaniment. The background is clean and slightly blurred, creating a modern bistro ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm pita bread for scooping.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large, oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 30 ml olive oil to skillet.
Add diced onion. Sauté 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and oregano. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in brown rice. Cook 2 minutes, stirring to coat.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Return chicken thighs to skillet.
Cover skillet. Reduce heat to low. Cook 30 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F) and rice is tender.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Add halved tomatoes and pitted olives to skillet.
Remove from heat. Let rest 5 minutes, covered.
Squeeze fresh lemon juice over dish. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley and crumbled feta cheese.
Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Beetroot and Goat Cheese Salad with Candied Walnuts
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a vibrant interplay of colors and textures.
