instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Slice red bell peppers into wide strips. Mince 2 garlic cloves. Toss bell pepper strips with 1 tablespoon olive oil, minced garlic, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes until tender and slightly charred. Remove from oven and set aside.
Cut chicken breasts into 2-3 cm chunks. Season chicken chunks with salt and pepper.

Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.

Add remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil to the same skillet. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 3-4 minutes. Add sliced mushrooms and cook until browned, about 5-7 minutes. Mince remaining 2 garlic cloves and add to skillet. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in diced tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Add roasted bell pepper strips. Let sauce simmer gently for 5-7 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta, reserving 125 ml of pasta water.
Add cooked pasta and seared chicken chunks to the sauce in the skillet. Toss to combine. If needed, add a little reserved pasta water to achieve desired sauce consistency.
Stir in most of the fresh basil leaves, roughly chopped. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. Stir in half of the grated Parmesan cheese.
Serve immediately, garnished with remaining fresh basil and grated Parmesan.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust the amount of chicken broth or reserved pasta water to achieve your preferred sauce consistency.
For extra flavor, a pinch of red pepper flakes can be added to the sauce with the garlic.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Biryani
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken Biryani served on a clean white porcelain plate. The dish features a mound of long-grain Basmati rice. The rice displays a natural color variation from pale white to deep orange-yellow from the spice infusion. Two large, bone-in chicken thigh chunks are nestled within the rice. The chicken is tender and coated in a thick, savory masala. Topping the rice are thin, golden-brown fried onion strips and vibrant green sprigs of fresh coriander. The arrangement is organic and centered with moderate negative space. A small ceramic bowl of white yogurt raita sits to the side. The background is a dark wood bistro table with a folded linen napkin and a polished brass spoon.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of cucumber raita
Accompany with lime wedges and sliced raw red onions
Traditional brass or copper serving spoon

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs, bone-in, cut into large chunks

instructions: Wash rice until water runs clear. Soak in water for 30 minutes.
Mix chicken chunks with yogurt, spice mix, ginger-garlic paste, and 5g salt. Marinate for 1 hour.
Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pot. Fry sliced onions until dark golden brown. Remove half for garnish.
Boil 1.5 L water with 10g salt. Add soaked rice. Cook until 70% tender. Drain immediately.
Add marinated chicken to the pot with remaining onions and ghee. Cook for 5 minutes over medium heat.
Layer the parboiled rice over the chicken chunks. Top with reserved fried onions, coriander, and mint.
Cover pot with a tight-fitting lid. Use a heavy weight or dough to seal steam inside.
Cook on very low heat for 25 minutes. Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Turn off heat. Let the pot rest for 10 minutes before opening.
Gently fluff the rice from the sides to mix colors without breaking grains.
notes: Do not overcook the rice during the initial boil or it will turn mushy during the steaming phase.
Use a heavy-bottomed pot (like a Dutch oven) to prevent the bottom layer of chicken from burning.

recipes.recipe_name: Celery and Roasted Chicken Salad with Lemon-Herb Vinaigrette
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a vibrant and artfully arranged composition. A bed of fresh, dark green spinach leaves forms the base, upon which thinly sliced, crisp green celery pieces are scattered. Bright red cherry tomato halves and translucent, very thinly sliced red onion rings provide pops of color and visual interest. Diced cucumber cubes add another layer of fresh green. Interspersed among the vegetables are small, irregular chunks of roasted chicken breast, displaying a lightly browned exterior and moist interior. A golden-green lemon-herb vinaigrette lightly coats all ingredients, with subtle pooling at the bottom of the plate. The entire arrangement is organic and flowing, with moderate negative space. A sprinkle of toasted almond slivers adds a textural contrast on top. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh textures and colors, with a soft, blurred restaurant-style background.

ingredients.name: Celery
ingredients.quantity: 4 stalks, thinly sliced on the bias

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Season chicken breast with salt and pepper. Roast until internal temperature reaches 75°C, about 20-25 minutes. Let cool. Cut into irregular 2 cm chunks.
Prepare vegetables. Thinly slice celery on the bias. Wash and dry spinach. Halve cherry tomatoes. Dice cucumber into 1 cm cubes. Very thinly slice red onion.
Prepare dressing. In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, lemon juice, Dijon mustard, chopped fresh dill, and chopped fresh parsley. Season with salt and black pepper.
In a large salad bowl, combine sliced celery, spinach, halved cherry tomatoes, diced cucumber, and thinly sliced red onion. Add the roasted chicken chunks.
Pour dressing over the salad ingredients. Toss gently to coat all components evenly.
Divide salad among four plates. Garnish each serving with toasted almond slivers. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Cordon Bleu with Dijon Cream Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and crisp, is cut diagonally into two thick pieces, revealing a molten core of thinly sliced smoked ham and melted Gruyère cheese. The chicken rests slightly off-center on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A creamy, pale yellow Dijon sauce is elegantly spooned around the base of the chicken, forming an appealing pool. A small sprig of fresh green parsley or finely chopped chives garnishes the dish, adding a pop of color. The overall presentation is professional and balanced, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. Standard silver flatware, a fork and knife, are placed neatly beside the plate. A folded cotton napkin rests nearby. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and colors of the dish. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere without distraction.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of steamed haricots verts (green beans) or roasted new potatoes.
Accompany with a crisp green salad dressed with a light vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Butterfly each chicken breast. Pound gently to an even thickness of about 1.5 cm.
Season chicken lightly with salt and pepper.
Place 2-3 slices of smoked ham and a few slices of Gruyère cheese on one half of each chicken breast.
Fold the other half over. Secure edges with toothpicks if needed.
Set up three dredging stations: one plate with flour, one bowl with beaten eggs, one plate with Panko breadcrumbs.
Dredge each chicken breast first in flour, shaking off excess. Then dip in egg, letting excess drip off. Finally, coat thoroughly in Panko breadcrumbs, pressing gently to adhere.
Heat butter and olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Add breaded chicken breasts to the hot skillet. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer skillet with chicken to the preheated oven. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
While chicken bakes, prepare the sauce. In a small saucepan, sauté finely diced onion in a teaspoon of oil until softened, about 3 minutes.
If using, deglaze with white wine, scraping up any browned bits. Reduce by half.
Stir in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Reduce by half.
Whisk in heavy cream and Dijon mustard. Simmer gently for 5-7 minutes, until sauce thickens slightly.
Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste. Keep warm.
Remove chicken from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes. Remove toothpicks.
Slice each chicken breast diagonally in half. Arrange on plates. Spoon Dijon cream sauce around chicken. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Pounding the chicken to an even thickness ensures even cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoky Yogurt Chicken with Skillet Flatbread
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Smoky Yogurt Chicken with Skillet Flatbread is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. A rustic, golden-brown skillet flatbread, slightly puffed and with visible char marks, rests on one side of the plate. Thick pieces of seared chicken, with a visible golden-brown crust and hints of creamy white yogurt marinade, are arranged naturally next to the flatbread. The chicken shows clear evidence of being cooked through. A sprinkle of bright green chopped parsley or chives adds a fresh accent. The setting is a well-used wooden dining table, with warm, cozy lighting, suggesting a relaxed family kitchen. A casually placed cloth napkin and standard flatware complete the homely, lived-in atmosphere. The background is minimal, keeping focus on the comfort food.
instructions: Combine 150g Greek yogurt, 5g hickory smoke salt, black pepper, garlic powder, and onion powder in a bowl. Mix well.
Add chicken thighs to the yogurt mixture. Coat thoroughly. Marinate for at least 30 minutes at room temperature, or up to 4 hours in the refrigerator.
For the flatbread dough, combine warm water, sugar, and yeast in a small bowl. Let sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy.
In a large bowl, whisk together whole wheat flour and 5g salt.
Add the bloomed yeast mixture, remaining 100g Greek yogurt, egg, and 15ml olive oil to the flour. Mix until a shaggy dough forms.
Turn dough onto a lightly floured surface. Knead for 5-7 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Lightly oil a clean bowl. Place dough in bowl, turn to coat. Cover with a clean cloth. Let rise in a warm place for 1 hour, or until doubled in size.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large cast-iron skillet or non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Remove chicken from marinade, shaking off excess. Place chicken in hot skillet. Sear for 5-7 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from skillet. Let rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.
While chicken rests, punch down flatbread dough. Divide into 4 equal portions. Roll each portion into a rough 20cm circle.

Heat the same skillet (or a clean one) over medium-high heat. Cook one flatbread at a time for 2-3 minutes per side, until puffed and lightly browned. Sprinkle a pinch of hickory smoke salt on each flatbread as it cooks.
Slice chicken into thick pieces.
Serve sliced chicken immediately with warm flatbreads. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley or chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Potato Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Chicken and Potato Skillet is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centered. A golden-brown, seared chicken thigh sits prominently. Rustic, tender potato wedges, their skins lightly crisped, are arranged around the chicken. Blistered, vibrant red cherry tomatoes are scattered among the potatoes and softened, caramelized red onion wedges. Melted, golden-brown Manchego cheese lightly coats the chicken and vegetables, adding a rich texture. Freshly chopped green parsley is sprinkled generously over the entire dish, providing a contrasting color and freshness. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a fork and knife, and a folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the flavorful pan juices.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt, pepper, and smoked paprika.
Halve small potatoes. Quarter red onion. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken thighs skin-side down in skillet. Sear 8-10 minutes until skin is golden and crispy. Flip chicken. Sear 2 minutes.
Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add potatoes and red onion to skillet. Sauté 5-7 minutes until slightly softened and browned.
Add minced garlic and dried oregano. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Return chicken to skillet, nestling among vegetables. Add cherry tomatoes and chicken broth.
Bring liquid to a simmer. Transfer skillet to preheated oven.
Bake 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C and potatoes are tender. Stir occasionally.
Grate Manchego cheese. Sprinkle over chicken and vegetables.
Return skillet to oven for 5 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes.
Chop fresh parsley. Garnish dish generously before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Garlic Herb Chicken with Rice Pilaf
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Garlic Herb Chicken is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Two golden-brown seared chicken thighs, cooked to tender perfection, are placed slightly overlapping towards the center. The chicken is generously coated with a rich, creamy off-white garlic sauce, speckled with finely diced, tender orange carrots and translucent pieces of sautéed onion. Beside the chicken, a neat, slightly mounded portion of fluffy white rice pilaf, subtly infused with fresh green chopped parsley, sits invitingly. A light drizzle of the creamy sauce pools around the base of the chicken and on the plate, adding to the visual appeal. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of vibrant green fresh parsley. The setting is a modern bistro table with a simple wooden surface, a crisp white cotton napkin folded neatly beside the plate, and standard silver flatware. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting colors.
instructions: Prepare chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Sear chicken: Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken until golden brown on both sides, about 4-5 minutes per side. Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Sauté aromatics: Add diced onion to the same pan. Sauté until softened, about 3 minutes. Add minced garlic and diced carrots. Sauté for another 3-4 minutes until slightly tender.
Deglaze: Pour in white wine (if using), scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Reduce liquid by half, about 2 minutes.
Add broth and herbs: Stir in chicken broth and fresh thyme leaves. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer.
Create sauce: Reduce heat to low. Whisk in mayonnaise until the sauce is smooth and creamy. Do not boil the sauce after adding mayonnaise.
Return chicken: Return seared chicken thighs to the pan, nestling them into the sauce. Simmer gently for 2-3 minutes to warm chicken through and coat with sauce.

Cook rice: While chicken simmers, prepare the rice. Rinse rice thoroughly under cold water. Combine rinsed rice with 600ml water and a pinch of salt in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork and stir in half of the chopped fresh parsley.

Serve: Plate a generous portion of the herb rice pilaf. Place one or two creamy garlic chicken thighs beside the rice. Spoon additional sauce, carrots, and onions over the chicken and rice. Garnish with the remaining fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rustic chicken cacciatore served in a shallow, cream-colored ceramic bowl with minor surface imperfections. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are the centerpiece, their skin appearing dark golden and tender from braising. The chicken is partially submerged in a thick, chunky tomato sauce featuring visible pieces of softened translucent onions and whole black olives. A single fresh rosemary sprig is placed casually on top. The bowl sits on a weathered dark wood kitchen table. Beside the bowl is a thick piece of torn crusty bread. The scene is illuminated by warm, soft overhead kitchen lighting, creating a cozy, authentic Italian home-dining atmosphere. A simple linen napkin and a stainless steel fork are placed to the left of the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty sourdough bread to soak up the tomato sauce
Pair with a side of simple polenta or rustic mashed potatoes
Traditional family-style dining involves placing the skillet in the center of the table
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden brown.
Flip chicken and sear for 4 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add crushed tomatoes, oregano, and the rosemary sprig.
Place chicken back into the skillet, nestled into the sauce.
Simmer on low heat for 30 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C internally.
Stir in the olives 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use bone-in thighs for maximum flavor and protein content
Ensure the sauce reduces until thick to concentrate the savory tomato profile
Always check the thickest part of the chicken for a safe internal temperature of 75°C

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Bacon Bread Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of golden-brown Cheesy Bacon Bread Bake is served on an everyday, slightly off-white ceramic plate. The baked strata, a roughly square cut from the casserole, features visible cubes of day-old bread, crispy crumbled bacon, and pockets of melted, bubbly cheddar cheese. Its top crust is beautifully browned and slightly crisp, contrasting with the soft, custardy interior. Beside the strata, a small, fresh green salad with mixed leaves provides a vibrant green counterpoint, adding a touch of freshness. The plate sits on a well-worn, natural wood dining table. A simple metal fork and knife are casually placed next to the plate. A soft, warm light from above illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting textures and colors. The background shows a hint of a lived-in kitchen, with a subtle blur of a wooden cutting board and simple salt and pepper shakers, reinforcing a homely atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad with vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease a 23x33 cm baking dish.
Cook diced bacon in a large skillet over medium heat until crisp. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Place on paper towels to drain. Reserve 15 ml bacon fat in the skillet.
Add butter to skillet with reserved bacon fat. Add diced onion. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute more until fragrant. Remove from heat.
In the prepared baking dish, combine bread cubes, cooked bacon, sautéed onion and garlic, and shredded cheddar cheese. Toss gently to distribute.
In a large bowl, whisk eggs, milk, salt, black pepper, and dried thyme until well combined.
Pour egg mixture evenly over bread mixture in the baking dish. Gently press down on bread to ensure all pieces are soaked.
Cover baking dish with foil. Refrigerate at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours, to allow bread to absorb custard.
Bake covered for 30 minutes.
Uncover. Continue baking 20-25 minutes, or until top is golden brown and a knife inserted into the center comes out clean.
Let stand 5-10 minutes before serving.
notes: For best results, use day-old bread. Fresh bread can become too soggy.
Soaking time is crucial for a custardy texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Sausage and Mushroom Tagliatelle with Roasted Cherry Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Tagliatelle pasta is elegantly coiled in a shallow, matte white ceramic pasta bowl, its strands evenly coated in a rich, rustic tomato sauce. Visible throughout the pasta are hearty, browned chunks of Italian sausage and earthy, sautéed cremini mushrooms. Scattered among the pasta are vibrant, slightly burst roasted cherry tomatoes, adding pops of red. Melted, irregular pieces of fresh mozzarella are draped over the top, creating a creamy contrast. The dish is garnished with a scattering of fresh green basil leaves, providing a fragrant, bright counterpoint. The composition is balanced, allowing for moderate negative space. The bowl rests on a light, natural wood table surface, accompanied by a simple silver fork and a folded off-white linen napkin. Natural, soft light illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and colors without harsh shadows.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette
Enjoy with a glass of dry red wine, such as Chianti
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss cherry tomatoes with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking tray. Roast for 15-20 minutes until softened and slightly burst. Set aside.

Remove sausage from casings. In a large skillet, heat 15 ml olive oil over medium-high heat. Add sausage, break into chunks. Cook, stirring occasionally, until browned and cooked through. Drain excess fat. Transfer sausage to a plate.
Add diced onion to the same skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are tender and browned, about 7-10 minutes.

Stir in tomato paste and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook for 1 minute. Pour in crushed tomatoes and broth. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
While sauce simmers, bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add tagliatelle pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente.

Drain pasta, reserving 125 ml pasta water. Add drained pasta to the sauce. Add roasted cherry tomatoes and grated Parmesan cheese. Toss to combine, adding reserved pasta water as needed to create a smooth sauce.
Serve immediately. Top each portion with torn fresh mozzarella and fresh basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Mushroom, White Bean, and Spinach Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented in a large, rustic ceramic serving bowl, placed centrally on a well-used wooden dining table. The colors are natural and inviting: vibrant green baby spinach forms the base, topped with earthy brown sautéed mushroom slices and creamy white cannellini beans. Bright red cherry tomato halves are scattered throughout, along with delicate rings of thinly sliced red onion. The components are casually mixed, allowing some ingredients to overlap naturally, creating a homely, comforting appearance. A light sheen from the Dijon vinaigrette coats the ingredients, making them look fresh and appetizing. The bowl is surrounded by a simple, slightly rumpled cloth napkin and basic, sturdy flatware, suggesting a relaxed family meal. Warm, soft light from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures of the ingredients. The overall impression is one of wholesome, expertly prepared home cooking, ready to be shared.
instructions: Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté until golden brown and tender, about 8-10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
In a small bowl, whisk together remaining 45 ml olive oil, Dijon mustard, and apple cider vinegar. Season with salt and pepper.
In a large serving bowl, combine baby spinach, rinsed white beans, thinly sliced red onion, and halved cherry tomatoes.
Add warm sautéed mushrooms to the salad bowl.
Pour dressing over the salad ingredients. Toss gently to combine all ingredients and coat with dressing.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chorizo, White Bean, and Tomato Braise
recipes.visual_description: The Spanish Chorizo, White Bean, and Tomato Braise is presented in a deep, pristine white ceramic bowl, showcasing its rich, rustic appeal. The hearty braise features plump, creamy white cannellini beans suspended in a vibrant, reddish-brown tomato sauce, infused with smoked paprika and a hint of saffron. Thick, seared rounds of Spanish chorizo, slightly caramelized at the edges, are interspersed throughout the beans. The sauce has a moderate thickness, clinging to the ingredients. A generous sprinkle of freshly chopped bright green flat-leaf parsley provides a fresh, aromatic contrast. The dish is centered on a simple wooden table with a white cotton napkin and standard flatware. A slice of crusty rustic bread rests beside the bowl, inviting dipping. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and deep colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with slices of crusty rustic bread, such as a baguette or Spanish pan rústico, for dipping into the flavorful sauce.
Accompany with a glass of robust Spanish red wine.

ingredients.name: Spanish Chorizo
ingredients.quantity: 300 g, sliced into 1 cm thick rounds

ingredients.name: Canned Cannellini Beans
ingredients.quantity: 2 x 400 g cans, rinsed and drained

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chorizo slices to the pot. Sear until browned and slightly crisp at the edges, about 2-3 minutes per side. Remove chorizo from pot with a slotted spoon. Set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot, using the rendered chorizo fat. Sauté until softened and translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic to the pot. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in smoked paprika and saffron threads (if using). Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
Pour in diced tomatoes and chicken stock. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer.
Add rinsed cannellini beans and the seared chorizo back into the pot.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer gently for 15-20 minutes, allowing flavors to meld and the sauce to thicken slightly.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Adjust seasoning as needed.
Ladle the hot braise into individual serving bowls. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Black Bean & Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of creamy, flowing Fermented Black Bean & Mushroom Risotto is centered on a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone. The risotto itself is a rich, warm beige, dotted with dark, glossy fermented black beans and varied shades of brown from the seared mushrooms. The mushrooms are presented in thick, natural slices and quartered pieces, integrated throughout the risotto, showcasing their rustic texture. Vibrant green wilted spinach leaves are gently folded in, providing pops of natural color and soft texture. The risotto has a fluid, natural consistency, spreading slightly on the plate, not constrained. A few irregular, golden-brown shards of crispy rice are artfully placed on top, adding a textural contrast and a subtle zero-waste nod. The plate sits on a light, textured bamboo surface. Adjacent are a simple, undyed linen napkin and a single, natural wooden spoon. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene from the side, highlighting the dish's textures. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of blurred natural greenery, reinforcing the sustainable theme.
instructions: Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Add mushrooms. Sear until golden brown, 5-7 minutes. Season lightly with salt. Set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the same pan. Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and coarsely chopped fermented black beans. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pan. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine, if using. Stir until fully absorbed.
Add one ladle of warm vegetable broth to the rice. Stir continuously until liquid is absorbed.
Continue adding broth, one ladle at a time, stirring constantly, until rice is creamy and al dente (18-20 minutes).
Remove from heat. Stir in seared mushrooms, nutritional yeast, and roughly chopped fresh greens. Stir until greens wilt.
Season with salt and pepper to taste. Ensure risotto is fluid.
Heat vegetable oil in a small pan over medium-high heat.
Add leftover cooked rice in a thin layer. Press down gently. Fry until golden brown and crispy on one side, 5-7 minutes.
Flip and crisp other side. Drain on paper towel. Break into irregular pieces.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Roasted Chicken with Potatoes and Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Tuscan Roasted Chicken is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thigh, left whole, is the focal point, positioned slightly off-center. Around the chicken, a scattering of roasted small potato halves or quarters, their skins slightly blistered and interiors tender, display varying shades of golden-brown. Interspersed among the potatoes are vibrant, burst red cherry tomato halves, some caramelized at the edges. Several smashed garlic cloves, soft and sweet, are visible. Fresh green sprigs of rosemary and thyme are artfully placed for color and aroma. A light sheen of pan juices coats the elements, reflecting the natural light. The arrangement is organic and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, suggesting a modern bistro setting. Beside the plate, a neatly folded light cotton napkin and standard silver flatware are arranged. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual restaurant atmosphere, with natural, even lighting illuminating the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up pan juices.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until deeply golden and crisp. Flip and sear for 2 minutes.
Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add remaining 30ml olive oil to the skillet. Add potatoes, smashed garlic, rosemary, and thyme.
Season potatoes with salt and pepper. Toss to coat.
Roast potatoes in the oven for 20 minutes.
Remove skillet from oven. Stir potatoes. Nestle chicken thighs back into the skillet among the potatoes.
Add halved cherry tomatoes around chicken and potatoes.
Pour white wine (or chicken broth) into the skillet.
Return skillet to oven. Roast for another 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and potatoes are tender and golden. Ensure chicken is cooked through.
Rest chicken 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: White Bean & Sourdough Fritters with Fermented Radish Slaw
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate with an organic, matte off-white finish, resting on a light reclaimed wood table. Three golden-brown, irregularly shaped White Bean & Sourdough Fritters are loosely stacked, showcasing their crispy exterior and rustic texture. Beside them, a small, dark, glossy dollop of Savory Bacon Jam gleams. A vibrant mound of Fermented Radish Slaw, composed of thinly sliced red radishes and finely shredded green cabbage, provides striking color contrast. The slaw is piled naturally. The entire plate is visible, with ample negative space. Garnish is minimal: delicate sprigs of fresh dill or fennel fronds are placed atop the slaw. The setting is clean, illuminated by soft, natural light, emphasizing the dish's natural ingredients and sustainable ethos. A simple, undyed linen napkin is folded beside the plate.
instructions: PREPARE FERMENTED RADISH SLAW (Start 3-5 days in advance): Thinly slice 200g radishes and 150g green cabbage using a mandoline or sharp knife. Combine 500ml non-chlorinated water and 10g sea salt to create brine. Submerge sliced vegetables in brine in a clean jar. Seal tightly. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days until desired tanginess. Refrigerate.

PREPARE SAVORY BACON JAM: Dice 100g smoked bacon into small chunks. Render bacon in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat until crispy. Remove bacon chunks, reserving rendered fat. Dice 1 medium red onion and 2 garlic cloves. Sauté red onion in reserved bacon fat until softened, about 5 minutes. Add garlic; cook 1 minute more. Deglaze pan with 120ml strong brewed coffee, scraping up browned bits. Add 30ml maple syrup and 15ml apple cider vinegar. Return crispy bacon to pan. Simmer on low heat for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until liquid reduces and mixture is thick and jam-like. Adjust seasoning. Set aside.

PREPARE FRITTER MIXTURE: Mash 400g cooked white beans in a large bowl. Process 150g day-old sourdough bread into coarse crumbs. Finely dice 1 small yellow onion and 2 garlic cloves. Sauté diced onion and garlic in 15ml olive oil until translucent. Add sautéed aromatics, sourdough crumbs, 30g nutritional yeast, 30g chopped fresh parsley, 5g salt, and 2g black pepper to mashed beans. In a small bowl, whisk 15g flaxseed meal with 45ml water; let sit 5 minutes to thicken. Add flax egg to bean mixture. Mix well to combine all ingredients.

FORM AND COOK FRITTERS: Divide mixture into 12 equal portions. Form each portion into a flattened patty, about 2 cm thick. Heat 45ml olive oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium heat. Cook fritters in batches for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and crispy. Drain on paper towels.

PLATE AND SERVE: Arrange 3 fritters per plate. Place a dollop of savory bacon jam next to the fritters. Add a generous portion of pre-fermented radish slaw. Garnish with fresh dill or fennel fronds. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe prioritizes using day-old bread, minimizing food waste.
Rendered bacon fat is reused for cooking.
Consider composting vegetable scraps for a truly zero-waste approach.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo e Manzo al Pomodoro con Peperoni e Parmigiano
recipes.visual_description: A generous portion of the hearty Pollo e Manzo al Pomodoro is presented centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Irregularly cut 3-4cm chunks of tender braised beef and succulent chicken are nestled within a rich, glossy, deep red tomato sauce. Vibrant 2cm wide strips of softened red and yellow bell peppers, along with diced onion, are integrated throughout, adding color and texture. Freshly grated pale yellow Parmesan cheese melts gently over the top. A few fresh, roughly torn green basil leaves are artfully placed for a final color contrast. The composition is naturally arranged, not overcrowded, with moderate negative space. The dish sits on a simple light wooden table in a modern bistro setting, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and classic silverware. Natural, even lighting highlights its rustic appeal against a softly blurred restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping
Serve over soft polenta or al dente pasta
Accompany with a simple green salad

ingredients.name: Large bell peppers (red, yellow, or orange)

instructions: Pat beef and chicken dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks until browned on all sides. Remove from pot.
Sear chicken chunks until browned on all sides. Remove from pot. Cook chicken to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and bell pepper strips. Cook 3 minutes until fragrant.
Deglaze with red wine, if using. Scrape up browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Reduce liquid by half.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, and dried oregano. Bring to a simmer.
Return beef and chicken to the pot. Stir well to combine.
Cover pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 1.5 hours, or until beef is tender. Stir occasionally.
Remove lid. Simmer uncovered for 15-20 minutes, or until sauce thickens slightly.
Stir in fresh basil.
Serve hot. Top each portion with grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: This dish can be made a day in advance. Flavors deepen overnight.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork Schnitzel with Warm Dill Potato Salad and Braised Apple Cabbage
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pork Schnitzel with Warm Dill Potato Salad and Braised Apple Cabbage is elegantly presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The golden-brown, crispy pan-fried pork schnitzel, a thinly pounded whole piece, is the focal point. Beside it, a vibrant mound of warm dill potato salad showcases neatly sliced potatoes, finely diced red onion, and cucumber, brightened by fresh green dill. A rich, deep purple braised apple cabbage, with visible shredded cabbage and diced apple pieces, complements the other elements. The colors are balanced and natural: the golden schnitzel, the green and white potato salad, and the deep purple cabbage create an appealing contrast. The plate is moderately spaced, allowing each component to be clearly seen without overcrowding. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, with a fork and knife placed beside the plate on a folded cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting that highlights the textures and colors of the food. A fresh lemon wedge and chopped parsley garnish the schnitzel, adding a pop of color and freshness.
instructions: Prepare Braised Apple Cabbage: Shred red cabbage thinly. Dice yellow onion finely. Core and dice apple into small cubes. In a large pot, heat a small amount of oil. Sauté diced yellow onion until translucent. Add shredded red cabbage, diced apple, honey, white wine vinegar, and water. Stir well. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat, cover, and cook for 30-40 minutes, or until cabbage is tender. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Prepare Warm Dill Potato Salad: Boil potatoes in salted water until fork-tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain and let cool slightly. Peel potatoes and slice into 1 cm thick rounds. Dice red onion finely. Dice cucumber into small cubes. Slice gherkins into thin rounds. Chop fresh dill. In a bowl, whisk together Dijon mustard, olive oil, apple cider vinegar, salt, and pepper. Gently combine sliced potatoes, diced red onion, cucumber, gherkins, and chopped dill with the dressing. Mix until well coated. Serve warm.

Prepare Pork Schnitzel: Slice pork loin into 4 equal portions. Place each portion between two sheets of cling film. Pound each pork portion evenly until very thin, about 3-4 mm thick. Set up three shallow dishes for breading: one with flour, one with beaten eggs, and one with breadcrumbs. Season pork cutlets with salt and pepper. Dredge each cutlet in flour, shaking off excess. Dip into beaten egg, ensuring full coverage. Finally, coat generously with breadcrumbs, pressing gently to adhere. Heat vegetable oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat until shimmering. Fry schnitzels in batches for 3-4 minutes per side, or until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Drain cooked schnitzels on a wire rack lined with paper towels. Season immediately with a pinch of salt.

Plate the dish: On each clean white porcelain dinner plate, arrange a portion of warm braised apple cabbage. Place a serving of warm dill potato salad beside the cabbage. Top with a crispy pork schnitzel. Garnish with a fresh lemon wedge and a sprinkle of chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Spinach and Feta Bread Pudding
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous square portion of Savory Spinach and Feta Bread Pudding is centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The pudding has a beautiful golden-brown, slightly puffed crust, indicating its perfect bake. Beneath the crust, the interior reveals distinct, soft cubes of sourdough bread, generously interspersed with vibrant green wilted spinach and creamy white crumbles of feta cheese. The texture appears custardy and moist, with the bread fully saturated. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley adorns the top. The plate is set on a simple wooden table surface, characteristic of a modern bistro. A neatly folded cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, creating a warm and inviting atmosphere. The background is minimal and slightly blurred, keeping the focus entirely on the inviting dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with a lemon vinaigrette.
Offer a side of Kalamata olives.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Grease a 23x33 cm baking dish with butter.
Cut stale sourdough bread into 2-3 cm cubes. Distribute evenly in the prepared baking dish.
Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add diced yellow onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic to the skillet. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add fresh spinach to the skillet. Cook, stirring, until spinach wilts completely. Remove from heat. Squeeze out excess liquid from the spinach.
In a large bowl, whisk together eggs, milk, salt, pepper, and grated nutmeg until well combined.
Sprinkle the wilted spinach and crumbled feta cheese evenly over the bread cubes in the baking dish.
Pour the egg and milk mixture over the bread, spinach, and feta. Gently press down on the bread cubes to ensure they absorb the liquid.
Let stand for 15 minutes to allow the bread to soak.
Bake for 40-45 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and the center is set. A knife inserted into the center should come out clean.
Remove from oven. Let cool for 10 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Black Pepper Cacio e Pepe with Braised Greens
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of spaghetti, twirled into a natural, slightly elevated mound, sits centered on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate. The pasta is coated in a rich, creamy, emulsified sauce, flecked generously with dark, coarsely ground black pepper. A small, artful cluster of vibrant, braised dark green Swiss chard or kale leaves rests gently beside the pasta, adding a pop of contrasting color and texture. The overall presentation is minimalistic, highlighting the pure ingredients. The plate is placed on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. A natural, undyed linen napkin is folded simply beside the plate. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene from the side, emphasizing the pasta's sheen and the greens' texture. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a hint of an earthy-toned wall or a blurred natural plant element.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately, as the sauce can tighten as it cools.
Traditionally eaten with a fork, twirling the pasta.
A simple crusty bread can be served alongside to mop up any remaining sauce.

ingredients.name: Seasonal greens (e.g., Swiss chard, kale), roughly chopped
Vegetable scraps (carrots, celery, onion peels, herb stems) for broth

instructions: Prepare concentrated vegetable broth: Combine vegetable scraps with 750 ml water in a pot. Simmer for 30 minutes. Strain. Reduce broth over medium-high heat until approximately 200 ml remains. Set aside.

Prepare fermented black pepper paste: Grind 10 g black peppercorns coarsely. Mix with 15 ml brine from another lacto-ferment (e.g., sauerkraut or pickle jar). Stir well. (Note: For best results, this paste should be prepared days in advance and fermented. For immediate use, a quick blend with a touch of vinegar can simulate tang.)
Cook pasta: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add pasta. Cook according to package instructions until al dente. Reserve 250 ml pasta water. Drain pasta.

Toast pepper: While pasta cooks, toast remaining 10 g whole black peppercorns in a dry, wide pan over medium heat for 2-3 minutes until fragrant. Grind coarsely using a mortar and pestle or spice grinder. Set aside a small amount for garnish.

Braise greens: In the same wide pan, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add chopped greens. Sauté until wilted. Add 50 ml of the concentrated vegetable broth. Braise until tender, about 5-7 minutes. Season lightly with salt. Remove greens from pan and set aside.
Make sauce: In the same pan (no need to clean), combine toasted ground pepper, fermented black pepper paste, and 50 ml of the reserved pasta water. Stir to combine.

Emulsify sauce (Mantecatura): Add grated Pecorino Romano to the pan. Gradually add remaining reserved pasta water and concentrated vegetable broth, stirring vigorously with tongs or a whisk. Continuously stir and toss to create a creamy, emulsified sauce. The consistency should be fluid and coats the back of a spoon.
Combine: Add cooked pasta to the sauce in the pan. Toss vigorously to coat all pasta strands evenly. If the sauce is too thick, add a tiny splash more hot water.
Plate: Serve pasta immediately, twirling into individual portions. Top each serving with the braised greens. Garnish with reserved fresh ground black pepper.
notes: The lacto-fermented black pepper paste adds a unique depth, tang, and umami to the dish, enhancing the classic Cacio e Pepe flavor profile.
Adjust the amount of pasta water and broth to achieve your desired sauce consistency. The sauce should be creamy and fluid, not dry.
This recipe champions zero-waste by utilizing vegetable scraps for a flavorful, concentrated broth and incorporates fermentation for enhanced flavor and complexity.

recipes.recipe_name: Japanese Beef and Potato Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Japanese Beef and Potato Stew is presented in a deep, traditional ceramic donburi bowl, showcasing a rich, savory broth. Tender, bite-sized beef chunks (approximately 5cm) are nestled amongst large, irregular potato chunks (4cm), vibrant orange carrot rounds (3cm), and soft white onion wedges. The ingredients are gently simmered, maintaining their distinct shapes and natural colors, with the beef exhibiting a slight caramelization from initial searing. A scattering of bright green chopped spring onions garnishes the top, adding a fresh contrast. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a small, perfectly steamed white rice bowl and a pair of dark wooden chopsticks. Natural, even lighting highlights the stew's comforting warmth and inviting texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with steamed white rice
Accompanied by miso soup
Traditionally paired with tsukemono (Japanese pickled vegetables)
instructions: Cut beef into 5cm bite-sized pieces. Cut potatoes into 4cm irregular chunks. Cut carrots into 3cm thick rounds. Cut onion into 8 wedges.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add beef. Sear until lightly browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd. Remove beef from pot. Set aside.
Add onion wedges to the same pot. Sauté until translucent, about 3-4 minutes.
Return beef to the pot. Add potatoes and carrots.
Pour in dashi stock, soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar. Bring to a boil.
Skim any foam or scum that rises to the surface.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot. Simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until vegetables are tender and beef is cooked through.
If using shirataki noodles, add them during the last 10 minutes of simmering.
Taste and adjust seasonings if necessary.
Serve hot. Garnish with chopped green onions.
notes: This dish tastes even better the next day as flavors meld.
Adjust sugar and soy sauce to taste based on personal preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Rigatoni with Sausage and Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of baked rigatoni, presented in a rustic white porcelain gratin dish. The top layer features golden-brown, bubbly melted mozzarella cheese, revealing hints of rich red tomato sauce and tender, browned Italian sausage chunks beneath. Sliced cremini mushrooms are interspersed throughout. The rigatoni pasta is al dente, holding the savory sauce. A sprinkle of vibrant green, fresh basil leaves and chopped parsley contrasts beautifully with the warm colors. The dish sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and depth of the dish, creating an inviting, comforting appearance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Enjoy with a glass of dry red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.

Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add crumbled Italian sausage. Brown sausage, breaking it apart. Cook until no pink remains. Remove sausage with a slotted spoon. Set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms. Cook until tender and lightly browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until wine mostly evaporates.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and browned sausage. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20 minutes, allowing flavors to meld. Season with salt and pepper.
While sauce simmers, cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta.
Add drained pasta to the sauce. Stir well to combine. Add half of the grated Parmesan cheese.
Transfer half of the pasta mixture to a 23x33 cm baking dish. Distribute half of the cubed mozzarella over the pasta.
Add remaining pasta mixture to the dish. Top with remaining mozzarella and remaining Parmesan cheese.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until cheese is bubbly and golden brown.
Let rest 5 minutes. Garnish with fresh basil and parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure sausage is well browned for maximum flavor development.
For best results, use good quality Italian crushed tomatoes.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Garlic Parmesan Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast, cooked whole, is the focal point on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. It is generously coated with a creamy, pale ivory garlic Parmesan sauce, which pools invitingly around its base. The chicken displays a crisp, caramelized exterior from searing. Freshly chopped vibrant green parsley is scattered over the chicken and sauce, providing a pop of color and freshness. The dish is presented on a light, natural wood table surface, with a folded off-white cotton napkin beside the plate. Traditional silver flatware is placed neatly alongside. The background is a subtly blurred modern bistro setting. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich textures and warm tones. The arrangement is professional, balanced, and approachable, with moderate negative space on the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of pasta, polenta, or crusty Italian bread to soak up the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt, pepper, and Italian herbs.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side. Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add shallot to skillet. Sauté 2 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits. Reduce by half.
Stir in heavy cream and Parmesan cheese. Whisk until smooth. Simmer 2-3 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.
Return chicken to skillet. Spoon sauce over chicken.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tomato Chicken Fettuccine
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Creamy Tomato Chicken Fettuccine is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The fettuccine is twirled into a neat mound, generously coated in a vibrant, creamy orange-red tomato sauce. Interspersed throughout the pasta are golden-brown, seared 2-3 cm chicken cubes, showcasing their tender interior and cooked exterior. A scattering of bright green, roughly torn fresh basil leaves provides a fresh counterpoint to the rich sauce. A light dusting of finely grated white Parmesan cheese rests atop the dish. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space on the plate. The scene is set on a simple wooden table, with standard European flatware and a folded cotton napkin positioned beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, unobtrusive restaurant-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread.
Pair with a simple green salad with vinaigrette.
instructions: Cut chicken breasts into 2-3 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add fettuccine. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250 ml pasta water before draining.

While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken cubes. Sear chicken until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add finely diced onion to the same pan. Sauté until softened, about 3-4 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, to thicken slightly.
Stir in heavy cream. Return chicken to the pan. Simmer for 2-3 minutes.

Add drained fettuccine to the pan with the sauce and chicken. Add half of the grated Parmesan. Toss to coat pasta evenly. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, a little at a time, until desired consistency is reached.
Toss in most of the fresh basil leaves, torn or roughly chopped.
Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining Parmesan and fresh basil.
notes: Ensure chicken is fully cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Adjust sauce consistency with reserved pasta water as needed.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato and Pickled Onion Salad
recipes.visual_description: An individual portion of the Potato and Pickled Onion Salad is presented on a handcrafted, natural cream-colored ceramic plate with a slight organic rim, resting on a light-toned reclaimed wood surface. Diced roasted potatoes, with their rustic, golden-brown skins and creamy interiors, are scattered throughout. Small, irregular pieces of shredded chicken are nestled amongst the vegetables, providing a subtle protein element without dominating the plate. Vibrant green mixed salad greens form the base, interspersed with thin, translucent slices of bright pink pickled red onions and crisp, thinly sliced red radishes. Fresh green dill sprigs are gently placed as a natural garnish. A light, glistening dressing coats the ingredients, highlighting their natural textures. The composition is clean and minimalist, with ample negative space around the central mound of salad. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural light, creating gentle shadows. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is casually draped nearby, and a subtle green plant is visible in the clean, uncluttered background, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.
instructions: Thinly slice the red onion. Place in a heatproof jar.

In a small saucepan, combine water, white vinegar, sugar, and 1 teaspoon salt. Bring to a boil, stirring until sugar and salt dissolve. Pour hot pickling liquid over red onions. Let cool, then refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

Preheat oven to 200°C. Wash and quarter the baby potatoes. Toss with 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 20-25 minutes until tender and golden brown. Let cool.
Season chicken breast with salt and pepper. Cook in a pan over medium heat for 6-8 minutes per side, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Shred or dice the cooked chicken. Let cool.
In a small bowl, whisk together remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil, apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper to make the dressing.
In a large bowl, combine mixed salad greens, diced roasted potatoes, shredded chicken, thinly sliced radishes, and chopped fresh dill.
Drain the pickled red onions and add to the salad. Pour dressing over the salad. Gently toss to combine. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Buckwheat Risotto with Roasted Chicken and Fermented Tomato Relish
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of creamy buckwheat risotto is centrally mounded on a round, handcrafted ceramic plate in a warm cream tone, leaving ample white space around the edges. The risotto, a rich earthy brown, is studded with tender, irregular chunks of roasted chicken, showcasing its natural golden-brown crust. Small, vibrant red pieces of fresh tomato are dispersed throughout, adding pops of color. A spoonful of bright, reddish-orange fermented tomato relish, with visible diced onion and garlic, rests atop the risotto, providing a contrasting texture and fresh acidity. Crispy, golden-brown bacon bits are scattered lightly over the top. The dish is garnished simply with fresh, finely chopped green parsley. The plate sits on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. A natural undyed linen napkin is folded beside it. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the organic textures and natural colors of the sustainable ingredients. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of green from a potted plant.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Tomato Relish: Dice 300g tomatoes, half onion, 2 cloves garlic. Mix with 5g salt. Place in a clean jar. Cover loosely. Let ferment at room temperature for 2-3 days until slightly bubbly and tangy. Stir daily. Refrigerate after desired tanginess.

Roast Chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper. In a bowl, toss chicken with 15ml soy sauce and 15ml olive oil. Roast at 200°C for 25-30 minutes, until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Let rest 5 minutes. Cut into 3-4 cm chunks.

Start Risotto: In a large pot, render diced bacon over medium heat until crispy. Remove bacon, reserve fat. Add 15g margarine and 15ml olive oil to the pot. Add remaining diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add remaining minced garlic, cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Cook Buckwheat: Add buckwheat groats to the pot. Toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly. Pour in 100ml chicken stock. Stir until absorbed.

Build Risotto: Add remaining chicken stock, 150ml at a time. Stir frequently. Wait until stock is mostly absorbed before adding more. Continue until buckwheat is tender but still has a slight bite (al dente), about 20-25 minutes. You may not need all stock.

Finish Risotto: Stir in remaining 15g margarine and grated Parmesan cheese. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. The risotto should be creamy and free-flowing. Stir in 200g diced fresh tomatoes (from the remaining 500g).
Assemble: Gently fold roasted chicken chunks and crispy bacon into the buckwheat risotto.
Serve: Ladle risotto onto plates. Top each portion with a spoonful of fermented tomato relish. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Utilize chicken bones and vegetable scraps to make homemade chicken stock for a zero-waste approach.
The fermented tomato relish enhances flavor and extends shelf life. Any leftover relish can be used as a condiment for other dishes.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato & Tomato Terrine with Fermented Cucumber Salsa Verde
recipes.visual_description: A refined, rectangular slice of Potato & Tomato Terrine stands proudly centered on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate. The terrine displays distinct, clean layers of thinly sliced, subtly roasted potatoes and vibrant red tomatoes, interspersed with a textured, earthy green lentil layer. Its edges are sharp, showcasing precise knife work. A small, vibrant green dollop of Fermented Cucumber Salsa Verde is artfully placed beside the terrine, adding a pop of fresh color and texture. The plate's natural, unglazed texture contrasts with the terrine's smooth surface. The overall composition emphasizes clean lines and natural ingredient beauty, with ample negative space. The setting features a light, textured stone surface, an undyed linen napkin, and soft, natural light illuminating the dish, with a subtle, blurred green plant in the background, reinforcing a sustainable aesthetic.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Cucumber:

Slice half cucumber into thin rounds. Place in a clean jar. Add 10g salt and cover with filtered water. Add 15ml apple cider vinegar. Seal jar. Ferment at room temperature for 2-3 days, or quick pickle for 24 hours in refrigerator.
Prepare Lentil Layer:

Rinse lentils. Cook lentils in 500ml vegetable broth until tender, about 20 minutes. Drain any excess liquid. Mash lightly. Mince 2 garlic cloves. Finely chop 15g dill and 15g parsley. Stir into lentils with 15ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Prepare Potatoes:
Wash potatoes thoroughly. Do not peel. Slice potatoes into 2mm thick rounds using a mandoline. Blanch potato slices in boiling salted water for 2 minutes. Drain well. Pat dry.
Prepare Tomatoes:
Wash tomatoes. Slice tomatoes into 3mm thick rounds.
Assemble Terrine:

Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a 25cm x 10cm loaf pan with parchment paper, leaving overhang on sides. Arrange a single layer of potato slices, slightly overlapping, on bottom of pan. Season lightly with salt and pepper. Add a layer of tomato slices. Spread half of the lentil mixture evenly over tomatoes. Repeat layers: potatoes, tomatoes, remaining lentil mixture, then finish with a final layer of potatoes.
Bake Terrine:

Cover terrine with parchment paper, then foil. Place a heavy object (like another loaf pan with cans) on top to press. Bake for 60 minutes. Remove foil and weight. Bake for another 20 minutes until potatoes are tender. Let cool completely in pan. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, with weight still on top.
Prepare Salsa Verde:

Drain fermented cucumber. Mince remaining 2 garlic cloves. Roughly chop remaining 15g dill and 15g parsley. Combine fermented cucumber, garlic, dill, parsley, 45ml olive oil, and remaining 15ml apple cider vinegar in a food processor. Pulse until a coarse salsa forms. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve:
Remove terrine from pan using parchment paper overhang. Slice terrine into 2cm thick portions. Serve each portion with a generous spoonful of Fermented Cucumber Salsa Verde on the side.
notes: This recipe embraces zero-waste by utilizing potato skins and minimizing food scraps.
The fermentation of cucumber adds depth of flavor and promotes gut health.

recipes.recipe_name: Rigatoni with Roasted Cherry Tomatoes and Crispy Pancetta
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Rigatoni with Roasted Cherry Tomatoes and Crispy Pancetta is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally mounded. The al dente rigatoni is coated in a rustic, vibrant sauce, showcasing burst and caramelized roasted cherry tomatoes. Diced, golden-brown crispy pancetta pieces are visibly distributed throughout the pasta. Fresh, torn green basil leaves are scattered over the top, providing a striking color contrast. A generous dusting of grated Pecorino Romano cheese covers the dish. The textures are a pleasing mix of tender pasta, soft tomatoes, and crunchy pancetta. The plate sits on a simple wooden table with a silver fork and a folded cotton napkin beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish’s inviting colors and textures, creating a professional yet approachable presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with additional grated Pecorino Romano or Parmigiano Reggiano at the table
Accompany with crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Place cherry tomatoes on a baking sheet. Drizzle with 15ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Roast for 20-25 minutes, until tomatoes burst and caramelize.
While tomatoes roast, cook pancetta in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook until crispy. Remove pancetta with a slotted spoon. Reserve rendered fat in skillet.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to skillet if needed. Add sliced garlic and chili flakes to skillet. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown garlic.
Cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250ml pasta cooking water before draining.
Add roasted cherry tomatoes to the skillet with garlic and chili. Gently mash some tomatoes to create a rustic sauce.
Add drained rigatoni to the skillet. Add reserved pasta water gradually, tossing constantly to create a cohesive sauce that coats the pasta.
Stir in crispy pancetta and most of the torn basil. Toss to combine.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with fresh Pecorino Romano and remaining torn basil.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Potato Tomato Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of a Rustic Chicken and Potato Tomato Bake is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate with a slightly raised rim, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. The plate holds one golden-brown roasted bone-in chicken thigh, nestled amongst thick, roasted potato wedges and tender, burst cherry tomato halves. Roughly chopped red onion and smashed garlic cloves are interspersed throughout the dish, all glistening lightly from olive oil. A scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley provides a final touch. The chicken skin is slightly crispy, the potatoes show soft interiors and lightly browned edges. The overall arrangement is natural and casual, with components touching and overlapping, reflecting a comforting, home-cooked meal. The scene is lit by warm, cozy light, suggesting a relaxed family dinner. A casually placed, folded beige linen napkin and a simple water glass sit nearby. The background is slightly blurred, hinting at a lived-in kitchen environment.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season chicken generously with salt and pepper.
Cut potatoes into thick wedges. Halve cherry tomatoes. Cut red onion into thick wedges. Smash garlic cloves.
In a large roasting pan, combine potato wedges, halved cherry tomatoes, red onion wedges, and smashed garlic.
Drizzle vegetables with olive oil. Sprinkle with dried oregano, salt, and pepper. Toss to coat evenly.
Nestle seasoned chicken thighs among the vegetables in the pan. Pour chicken broth into the pan.
Bake for 35-45 minutes. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C. Potatoes should be tender and lightly browned.
Remove pan from oven. Let the bake rest for 5 minutes.
Chop fresh parsley. Garnish the bake with chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken with Preserved Lemon & Seasonal Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: Single roasted chicken thigh, golden-brown and crisp-skinned, placed slightly off-center on a round, handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural cream tone. Around the chicken, arrange generous, rustic chunks of roasted carrots, parsnips, and potato wedges, interspersed with vibrant green broccoli florets. The vegetables show slight charring and tender edges. A generous sprinkle of bright green preserved lemon and herb gremolata rests atop the chicken and a few scattered pieces on the vegetables. The plate rests on a light, reclaimed wood surface. A natural, undyed linen napkin is folded loosely beside it. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene from the side, creating gentle shadows. Background is minimalist, perhaps a subtle out-of-focus plant.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and cut carrots and parsnips into thick chunks. Cut potatoes into wedges. Cut broccoli into florets.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Arrange chicken thighs, carrot chunks, parsnip chunks, and potato wedges on a large baking tray. Drizzle with olive oil. Add 2 crushed garlic cloves to the tray. Roast for 30 minutes.
After 30 minutes, add broccoli florets to the tray. Continue roasting for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and vegetables are tender-crisp.
While chicken roasts, finely chop the preserved lemon rind (discard pulp). Finely chop fresh parsley and mint. Mince the remaining fresh garlic clove.
Combine chopped preserved lemon, parsley, mint, and minced garlic in a small bowl to make the gremolata.
Remove chicken and vegetables from oven. Let chicken rest for 5 minutes.
Plate a roasted chicken thigh with an assortment of roasted vegetables. Spoon gremolata over the chicken and vegetables. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe emphasizes using seasonal produce. Adjust vegetables based on availability.
Save vegetable scraps and chicken bones to make homemade stock, reducing food waste.
Preserved lemons can be made at home from excess lemons, enhancing the zero-waste approach.

recipes.recipe_name: Paneer Makhani Curry
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Paneer Makhani Curry is presented in a deep, pristine white porcelain bowl. The curry itself is a vibrant, rich orange-red, its smooth, velvety gravy glistening from the butter and cream. Generous 2cm cubes of light golden-brown paneer are nestled within the sauce, some peeking out. The dish is garnished with a generous sprinkle of bright green, freshly chopped coriander leaves, and a delicate swirl of fresh cream on top. The bowl sits on a simple light wooden table. Beside it, a small, elegant white porcelain bowl holds fluffy, perfectly cooked basmati rice. A warm, folded piece of garlic naan bread rests gracefully beside the main bowl. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even light, creating a professional yet inviting atmosphere, with a subtle, blurred restaurant-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with basmati rice, naan bread, or roti.
Accompaniments such as raita (yogurt dip) or pickled onions are common.
instructions: Soak cashew nuts in hot water for 20 minutes. Drain. Blend cashews with 50ml fresh water to a very smooth paste. Set aside.
Heat 15ml oil in a separate non-stick pan over medium heat. Lightly pan-fry paneer 2cm cubes until golden on all sides. Remove and set aside.
In a large heavy-bottomed pan, heat butter and remaining 15ml oil over medium heat.
Add cumin seeds. Let them splutter, about 10 seconds.
Add finely diced onion. Sauté until translucent and lightly golden, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Reduce heat to low. Add turmeric powder, coriander powder, and red chili powder. Stir for 30 seconds.
Pour in tomato puree. Add salt and sugar (if using). Increase heat to medium. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the mixture thickens and oil begins to separate from the sides, about 10-15 minutes.
Stir in the prepared cashew paste. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly to prevent sticking.
Add 150ml water. Bring the gravy to a gentle simmer. Cook for 5 minutes.
Gently add the pan-fried paneer cubes to the simmering gravy. Simmer for another 5 minutes.
Stir in garam masala and crushed kasuri methi.
Remove the pan from heat. Stir in the fresh cream.
Garnish generously with fresh chopped coriander leaves. Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken, Mushroom, and Tomato Rice Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Hearty Chicken, Mushroom, and Tomato Rice Bake is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The dish features tender, golden-brown chicken chunks nestled within a creamy, tomato-infused rice mixture. Soft, earthy brown mushroom slices and bright red diced tomatoes are visibly integrated throughout the rice. The top is covered with a golden, bubbly layer of melted cheddar cheese, with some crispy edges. The rice has absorbed the broth, maintaining a moist, comforting texture, not dry. A few flecks of green from optional fresh parsley garnish are scattered on top. The plate is placed on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple fork and knife rest beside the plate. The scene is bathed in warm, inviting kitchen lighting, evoking a relaxed, lived-in family dining atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Slice mushrooms. Dice onion. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Brown on all sides. Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook for 3-5 minutes until mushrooms are tender.
Stir in uncooked rice, diced tomatoes (undrained), dried oregano, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Return browned chicken to the skillet. Nestle chicken into the rice mixture.
Cover the skillet tightly with a lid or foil. Transfer to the preheated oven.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until most liquid is absorbed and rice is tender.
Remove from oven. Sprinkle grated cheddar cheese evenly over the top.
Return to oven, uncovered. Bake for another 10-15 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly and lightly golden.
Let stand 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh parsley if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Mexican Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Hearty Mexican Chicken and Rice is presented on an everyday, slightly off-white ceramic plate with a subtle, rustic texture, resting on a well-used wooden dining table. The dish features a golden-brown, seared chicken thigh, nestled among fluffy, vibrant orange-red rice. The rice is studded with bright yellow corn kernels and finely diced red bell pepper and onion, creating a colorful, inviting texture. Fresh, chopped coriander leaves are scattered over the top, adding a pop of green. The chicken is whole, not sliced, showcasing its tender, cooked-through appearance. A lime wedge sits casually on the side of the plate. In the background, a simple, folded white cloth napkin and a rustic fork are visible. Warm, soft kitchen lighting casts gentle shadows, enhancing the comforting, homemade feel of the meal, with subtle, natural clutter visible on the table.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn or flour tortillas
Offer a side of salsa or pickled jalapeños
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear for another 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and red bell pepper to the pot. Cook for 5 minutes until softened, stirring occasionally.
Add minced garlic, ground cumin, dried oregano, and chili powder. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add uncooked rice to the pot. Stir well to coat the rice with the aromatics and spices. Toast rice for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in diced tomatoes (undrained) and chicken broth. Stir to combine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the rice mixture. Bring liquid to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover the pot tightly, and simmer for 20 minutes. Do not lift the lid.
Stir in frozen corn kernels. Re-cover and cook for another 5-10 minutes, or until all liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove pot from heat. Let it rest, covered, for 5-10 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped coriander. Serve hot with lime wedges.
notes: Allowing the rice to rest after cooking is crucial for a fluffy texture.
Adjust chili powder to your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Sweet and Savory Pork and Chicken Stir-Fry
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Sweet and Savory Pork and Chicken Stir-Fry is presented centrally on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The dish features an organized, yet natural mound of golden-brown seared chicken and pork cubes, intermingled with vibrant red and yellow bell pepper batons, succulent pineapple chunks, sliced cremini mushrooms, and bright green beans. Each ingredient retains its distinct shape and texture. A glossy, amber-hued sauce lightly coats the components, pooling slightly at the base. Freshly chopped green coriander is scattered over the top, adding a pop of color. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table surface and a cotton napkin positioned beside the plate. A small white rice bowl and chopsticks rest to the side, ready for serving. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish’s inviting colors and textures, with a clean, unobtrusive background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with steamed jasmine rice.
Use chopsticks for an authentic dining experience.
instructions: Cut chicken and pork into 2.5 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Cut bell peppers into 2 cm batons. Cut pineapple into 2.5 cm chunks. Slice mushrooms. Trim green beans.
Mince ginger and garlic.
In a small bowl, whisk together chicken stock, Dijon mustard, soy sauce, and cornstarch. Set aside.
Heat 15 ml vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat.
Add pork cubes. Sear until browned on all sides, about 4-5 minutes. Remove from wok. Set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml vegetable oil to the wok.
Add chicken cubes. Sear until browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove from wok. Set aside.
Add bell peppers, mushrooms, ginger, and garlic to the wok. Stir-fry for 3 minutes until fragrant and vegetables are crisp-tender.
Add green beans and pineapple chunks to the wok. Stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Return cooked chicken and pork to the wok.
Stir the prepared sauce mixture. Pour into the wok. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens, about 1-2 minutes.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Chop fresh coriander. Stir half into the stir-fry. Garnish with remaining coriander.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Roasted Corn & Bell Pepper Relish
