recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, with a golden-brown crust, rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is a whole, plump piece, positioned slightly off-center. Alongside it, a vibrant mound of roasted corn and bell pepper relish is spooned. The relish features bright yellow corn kernels, interspersed with small, diced pieces of red and yellow bell peppers and finely minced red onion, offering a colorful medley. A scattering of fresh, green cilantro leaves garnishes the relish. A fresh lime wedge sits beside the chicken. The dish exhibits natural, appealing colors and varied textures: the crispy exterior of the chicken against its tender interior, and the slightly charred corn kernels contrasting with the crisp-tender bell peppers. The plate is presented on a simple wooden table surface, with a cotton napkin and standard flatware, under natural, even lighting, creating a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt, pepper, and smoked paprika on both sides.
Prepare corn: Brush cobs lightly with olive oil. Grill or roast cobs until slightly charred and tender. Cut kernels off cobs.
Prepare relish vegetables: Dice red and yellow bell peppers into small cubes. Finely dice red onion. Mince garlic.

Sear chicken: Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Sear for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Let rest on a cutting board.
Make relish: In the same skillet, add remaining 15ml olive oil. Add diced bell peppers, red onion, and minced garlic. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Combine relish: Add roasted corn kernels to the skillet. Stir well. Cook for 2 minutes. Remove from heat. Stir in fresh lime juice and chopped cilantro. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Plate: Place one seared chicken breast on each plate. Spoon a generous portion of the roasted corn and bell pepper relish alongside the chicken. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken and Vegetable Pizza Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty Chicken and Vegetable Pizza Soup is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl, showcasing a rich, warm red-orange broth. Visible chunks of cooked chicken, diced red bell pepper, sliced mushrooms, and small pasta are generously distributed throughout the soup. The broth has a comforting, slightly thick texture. A simple sprinkle of grated Parmesan cheese melts gently on top, accompanied by a few fresh, vibrant green basil leaves. The bowl sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. A casual, red and white checkered cloth napkin is loosely placed beside the bowl. The setting evokes a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere with soft, natural overhead lighting. The overall presentation is homely and inviting, focusing on the comforting appeal of the soup. A piece of crusty Italian bread or a garlic knot is casually placed next to the bowl, ready for dipping.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread or garlic knots for dipping.
Pair with a simple green salad.
instructions: Dice chicken into 2 cm cubes. Dice onion and bell pepper. Slice mushrooms. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion and bell pepper. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add diced chicken. Cook until lightly browned on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Stir in minced garlic, sliced mushrooms, and dried oregano. Cook for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in diced tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a boil.
Add small pasta. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 10-12 minutes, or until pasta is tender.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle hot soup into individual bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped basil or parsley and a sprinkle of grated Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Chicken and Mushroom Pasta
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, showcasing a generous individual portion. A mound of al dente penne pasta, coated in a creamy, golden-white sauce, forms the base. Scattered throughout the pasta are tender, browned chicken chunks, irregularly shaped and substantial. Dark brown, sautéed mushroom slices are visible, adding depth and earthy tones. Vibrant green, roasted broccoli florets, some with slightly caramelized edges, are interspersed, providing a contrasting color and texture. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese covers the top, and fresh, bright green chopped parsley is sprinkled over the entire dish. The composition is organic and inviting, with a focus on the natural textures and colors of the ingredients. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface with a folded white cotton napkin beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish without harsh shadows.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with crusty Italian bread.
A simple green salad with a vinaigrette dressing complements the richness.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss broccoli florets with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes until tender-crisp and slightly charred.
Cook pasta according to package directions in salted water until al dente. Reserve 125ml pasta cooking water. Drain pasta.

While pasta cooks, season chicken chunks with salt and pepper. Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear until golden brown on all sides and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.

Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same skillet. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 3-4 minutes. Add sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms release their liquid and brown, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Stir in heavy cream. Simmer for 2-3 minutes until sauce slightly thickens.
Return cooked chicken to the skillet. Add cooked pasta. Toss to combine. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta cooking water, 30ml at a time, until desired consistency is reached.
Stir in grated Parmesan cheese and chopped parsley. Taste and adjust seasoning.
notes: For best results, use freshly grated Parmesan cheese.
Do not overcook the pasta; it should be al dente.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Cashew Macaroni with Roasted Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural earth tone, resting on a light bamboo table. A single refined portion occupies the center, surrounded by ample white space. Macaroni, coated in creamy, off-white fermented cashew sauce, forms a natural mound. Rustic, irregularly cut 2-3cm chunks of roasted root vegetables—carrots, parsnips, celeriac—are scattered around, displaying warm orange, pale yellow, and creamy white tones with light caramelization. The vegetables show tender, crinkled textures. Freshly ground black pepper flecks the sauce. A few small, bright green sprigs of fresh parsley provide subtle color contrast. The composition is clean, simple, and unforced, highlighting natural beauty. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is subtly visible.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Cashew Cream: Soak cashews in water for at least 4 hours, or overnight. Drain and rinse. Blend soaked cashews with 150ml fresh water, nutritional yeast, lemon juice, minced garlic, Dijon mustard, smoked paprika, and a pinch of salt until very smooth and creamy. If too thick, add more water gradually. Transfer to a clean jar. Cover loosely with a cloth or lid. Let ferment at room temperature for 12-24 hours, or until slightly tangy and bubbly. Refrigerate after fermentation.

Prepare Root Vegetables: Preheat oven to 200°C. Wash and peel root vegetables. Keep peels for broth. Cut vegetables into rustic 2-3cm chunks. Toss with olive oil, salt, and black pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 25-35 minutes, or until tender and slightly caramelized.
Prepare Zero-Waste Vegetable Broth: While vegetables roast, place all vegetable peels and scraps in a small pot. Add 500ml water. Simmer for 20-30 minutes to create a light broth. Strain and reserve.
Cook Macaroni: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add macaroni. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 100ml pasta water.

Combine Dish: In a large pan, gently heat the fermented cashew cream. Add cooked macaroni. Stir to coat. If sauce is too thick, add a little reserved pasta water or vegetable broth until desired consistency. Season with fresh black pepper and salt to taste.

Quick Pickled Scraps (Optional Garnish/Flavor): Take a small portion of root vegetable peels or other firm vegetable scraps. In a small bowl, mix apple cider vinegar, sugar, and a pinch of salt. Add scraps and let sit for at least 15 minutes.
Plate: Divide macaroni among 4 plates. Arrange roasted root vegetable chunks around or on top of the macaroni. Garnish sparingly with a few fresh herb sprigs or quick-pickled vegetable scraps.
notes: This recipe utilizes fermentation for depth of flavor and incorporates zero-waste principles by using vegetable scraps for broth or quick pickles. It is entirely plant-based and emphasizes seasonal, local ingredients.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: Serve the risotto on a flat white porcelain dinner plate. The consistency is fluid and spreads naturally across the plate, appearing free-flowing rather than molded. The rice grains are distinct, coated in a glossy, creamy sauce. Large 3cm chunks of golden-brown seared chicken thighs are distributed throughout the rice. Sliced cremini and shiitake mushrooms show deep caramelization and earthy brown tones. The dish features a pale golden hue. Finely minced flat-leaf parsley provides a vibrant green contrast. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese covers the surface. The arrangement is organic. Beside the plate sits a heavy silver spoon and a folded white cotton napkin on a light oak table. Natural side lighting highlights the creamy texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while the consistency remains fluid
Accompany with a crisp dry white wine such as Pinot Grigio
Provide extra grated Parmesan at the table
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3cm chunks.
Dice onion into 5mm pieces.
Mince garlic cloves.
Slice mushrooms into 5mm thick pieces.
Heat 20ml olive oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until browned and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add mushrooms to the same pan. Sauté until moisture evaporates and edges brown.
Remove mushrooms and set aside.
Melt 20g butter in the pan. Add onion and garlic.
Cook until softened but not browned.
Add rice. Stir 2 minutes to toast the grains until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until liquid is fully absorbed.
Add 200ml warm stock. Stir continuously until liquid is absorbed.
Repeat stock additions one ladle at a time, stirring constantly, until rice is tender but firm.
Return chicken and mushrooms to the pan.
Remove from heat.
Vigorously stir in remaining 30g butter and Parmesan cheese to create a creamy emulsion.
Season with salt and pepper. Fold in chopped parsley.
notes: Keep the chicken stock at a low simmer in a separate pot to maintain cooking temperature.
Stirring constantly is essential to release rice starches for a creamy texture.
Ensure chicken reaches the safety temperature of 75°C during the initial searing phase.

recipes.recipe_name: Coffee-Kissed Lemon Semifreddo with Toasted Breadcrumb Crunch
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Coffee-Kissed Lemon Semifreddo is elegantly presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a harmonious blend of creamy textures and vibrant flavors. The semifreddo, a rectangular slice approximately 2 cm thick and 8 cm long, stands proudly on the plate, revealing its pale yellow hue from the lemon base, beautifully streaked with rich, dark brown swirls of concentrated coffee. Its surface is smooth and slightly glossy, indicating its frozen, yet yielding, texture. A generous sprinkle of golden-brown, toasted breadcrumb crunch cascades around the base and atop the semifreddo, providing a delightful textural contrast. The plate features moderate negative space, allowing the dessert to be the focal point. A thin, delicate round slice of fresh lemon, about 3 cm in diameter, is placed beside the semifreddo, adding a pop of bright yellow and a fresh aromatic element. A small, vibrant green mint sprig provides a touch of contrasting color and freshness. The setting is a modern bistro, with the plate resting on a simple light wooden table. A folded cotton napkin is placed to the side, and the scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting, creating an inviting and refined dessert presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small espresso on the side.
Offer with biscotti for dipping.
Enjoy as a refreshing end to a multi-course Italian meal.
instructions: Prepare Breadcrumb Crunch: Melt butter in a pan over medium heat. Add breadcrumbs, sugar, and a pinch of salt. Cook, stirring constantly, until golden brown and crispy. Transfer to a plate. Let cool completely.
Prepare Coffee Swirl: Combine espresso and sugar in a small saucepan. Heat gently until sugar dissolves. Simmer briefly to reduce slightly, creating a concentrated syrup. Let cool.

Prepare Lemon Semifreddo Base: In a heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of simmering water (bain-marie), whisk egg yolks, 100g sugar, lemon zest, and lemon juice. Whisk constantly until mixture is pale, thick, and reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove from heat. Continue whisking until cool and very thick.
Whip Cream: In a separate cold bowl, whip heavy cream until medium-stiff peaks form.
Combine Semifreddo: Gently fold the whipped cream into the cooled egg yolk mixture until just combined.

Assemble Semifreddo: Pour half of the semifreddo mixture into a loaf pan (approx. 20x10 cm) lined with cling film, leaving overhang. Drizzle half of the cooled coffee swirl over the semifreddo. Gently swirl with a knife. Add remaining semifreddo mixture. Drizzle with remaining coffee swirl. Swirl gently.
Freeze: Cover with cling film. Freeze for at least 6 hours, or overnight, until firm.
Serve: Un-mold the semifreddo. Slice into 4 portions. Plate each slice. Sprinkle generously with toasted breadcrumb crunch. Garnish with a thin lemon slice and a mint sprig.
notes: Ensure the egg yolk mixture reaches 75°C for food safety.
Chill the mixing bowl and whisk for the cream for better whipping results.
Do not overmix when folding in the whipped cream; keep it light and airy.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Sausage and Potato Skillet with Fried Eggs
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of German Smoked Sausage and Potato Skillet is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Cubed potatoes are roasted to a golden-brown, mixed with thick rounds of pan-fried smoked sausage, diced caramelized onions, and vibrant red bell pepper. A perfectly fried egg, with a firm white and a rich, runny yellow yolk, rests atop the hearty mixture. The dish is garnished with a scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley. Textures include crispy potato edges, tender vegetables, and the smooth, creamy yolk. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table. A folded cotton napkin and traditional flatware are placed beside the plate. A small side bowl of tangy sauerkraut accompanies the dish, enhancing its authentic German presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with tangy sauerkraut
Offer a variety of German mustards (e.g., Dijon, whole grain)
Serve with pickled gherkins
instructions: Peel potatoes. Cut into 2 cm cubes.
Chop onion into 1 cm dice. Mince garlic.
Cut smoked sausage into 1.5 cm thick rounds.
Remove seeds from bell pepper. Cut into 1.5 cm dice.
Heat oil in large skillet over medium-high heat. Add potatoes. Cook 10-12 minutes until browned and tender. Stir occasionally.
Add smoked sausage, diced onion, and diced bell pepper to skillet. Cook 8-10 minutes until sausage is browned and vegetables are softened.
Add minced garlic and paprika. Cook 1 minute until fragrant. Season with salt and pepper.
Remove skillet from heat. Divide mixture into four portions.
In a separate pan, melt butter over medium heat. Fry eggs individually until whites are set and yolks are runny.
Plate one portion of skillet mixture onto each plate. Top each with a fried egg.
Chop fresh parsley. Garnish each plate with chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Garlic Chicken Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of Creamy Garlic Chicken Pasta is presented on a simple, off-white ceramic dinner plate. The penne pasta is coated in a rich, creamy, light-yellow sauce. Irregularly cut, golden-brown chicken chunks are interspersed throughout the pasta, showcasing their seared exterior and tender interior. Finely diced onion and minced garlic are visible within the sauce, alongside flecks of green dried oregano. A light sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley garnishes the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The dish is arranged naturally, with components touching and slightly overlapping, suggesting a comforting, home-cooked meal. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, alongside a standard fork. The scene is lit with warm, cozy lighting, evoking a relaxed family dining atmosphere with minimal, unobtrusive background elements.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 2.5 cm bite-sized chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Dice the onion finely. Mince the garlic cloves.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks to the pan. Cook until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add diced onion to the same pan. Sauté until softened, about 3-4 minutes.
Add minced garlic and dried oregano to the pan. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Stir in heavy cream and grated Parmesan cheese. Simmer gently for 5 minutes, until sauce thickens slightly.
Meanwhile, cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Add cooked pasta and cooked chicken chunks back into the sauce. Toss to combine.
Stir in fresh chopped parsley. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rustic chicken cacciatore served in a shallow, cream-colored ceramic bowl with minor surface imperfections. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are the centerpiece, their skin appearing dark golden and tender from braising. The chicken is partially submerged in a thick, chunky tomato sauce featuring visible pieces of softened translucent onions and whole black olives. A single fresh rosemary sprig is placed casually on top. The bowl sits on a weathered dark wood kitchen table. Beside the bowl is a thick piece of torn crusty bread. The scene is illuminated by warm, soft overhead kitchen lighting, creating a cozy, authentic Italian home-dining atmosphere. A simple linen napkin and a stainless steel fork are placed to the left of the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty sourdough bread to soak up the tomato sauce
Pair with a side of simple polenta or rustic mashed potatoes
Traditional family-style dining involves placing the skillet in the center of the table
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden brown.
Flip chicken and sear for 4 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add crushed tomatoes, oregano, and the rosemary sprig.
Place chicken back into the skillet, nestled into the sauce.
Simmer on low heat for 30 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C internally.
Stir in the olives 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use bone-in thighs for maximum flavor and protein content
Ensure the sauce reduces until thick to concentrate the savory tomato profile
Always check the thickest part of the chicken for a safe internal temperature of 75°C

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Bell Pepper & Basil Pasta with Ricotta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pasta is elegantly presented in a handcrafted ceramic bowl with an organic, slightly irregular shape, in an earthy cream or beige tone. The short pasta is coated in a vibrant, creamy orange-red sauce from the fermented bell peppers, showcasing subtle specks of color. A generous, soft dollop of pure white ricotta sits prominently on top, creating a striking contrast. Fresh, bright green basil leaves, some whole, some gently torn, are scattered naturally over the pasta and ricotta. Small, golden-brown crispy rice pieces provide textural counterpoint. The dish is clean and uncluttered, with ample negative space. The table surface is light, natural wood or stone. Lighting is soft, natural, and diffused, highlighting textures and colors. A simple, undyed linen napkin is casually placed beside the bowl. The entire plate is visible.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Bell Peppers: Wash and dice bell peppers into 2 cm pieces. Place in a clean 1-liter jar. Dissolve 15g salt and a pinch of sugar in 500ml filtered water to make brine. Pour brine over peppers, ensuring they are fully submerged (use a fermentation weight if available). Seal loosely or use an airlock lid. Ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Burp daily. Refrigerate once fermented.

Crisp Leftover Rice: Heat 10ml olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add cooked leftover rice and press into a thin layer. Cook until golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Break into small pieces. Set aside.

Prepare Bell Pepper Sauce: Drain 400g of the fermented bell peppers. Reserve 60ml of the fermentation brine. In a blender, combine drained bell peppers, 2 cloves minced garlic, 50ml olive oil, and 30ml reserved brine. Blend until smooth. Taste and adjust seasoning with black pepper or more brine if needed.
Cook Pasta: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add pasta and cook according to package instructions until al dente. Reserve 120ml of pasta cooking water before draining.

Combine & Finish: Return drained pasta to the pot. Add the bell pepper sauce and 60ml of the reserved pasta water. Stir well to coat, adding more pasta water if needed for desired consistency. Stir in half of the fresh basil leaves, roughly torn.

Plate & Serve: Divide pasta among four shallow bowls. Dollop each serving with 50g fresh ricotta. Grate Parmesan over the top. Garnish with remaining fresh basil leaves and crispy rice pieces. Drizzle with remaining 20ml olive oil and a pinch of chili flakes if desired.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste cooking. Bell pepper cores and basil stems can be used to make a light vegetable broth for other uses. Leftover cooked rice is repurposed into a crispy garnish.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Chicken & Fermented Tomato Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Sustainable Chicken & Fermented Tomato Pasta is presented on a round, handcrafted ceramic plate in a warm cream tone, centered on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. The pasta, a generous nest of al dente rigatoni, is coated in a vibrant, rustic red fermented tomato sauce. Nestled alongside the pasta are two substantial, golden-brown pan-seared chicken chunks, showing a crisp exterior. Scattered around are bright green, roughly chopped wilted seasonal greens and a few glistening, thinly sliced pickled carrot batons, adding a contrasting texture and color. A scattering of fresh, torn basil leaves provides a final aromatic garnish. The composition is clean and natural, with ample negative space. The setting is minimalist with an undyed linen napkin, illuminated by soft, natural overhead light, enhancing the dish's organic beauty.

ingredients.name: Vegetable scraps (e.g., carrot ends, zucchini trimmings) for pickling

instructions: Prepare Fermented Tomatoes: Roughly chop 500g ripe tomatoes. Place in a clean glass jar. Add 20g non-iodized salt. Cover with 500ml filtered water. Seal jar loosely. Let ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Burp daily. Refrigerate once fermented.

Prepare Pickled Vegetable Scraps: Thinly slice 100g vegetable scraps (e.g., carrot ends into batons, zucchini trimmings into rounds). In a small saucepan, combine 100ml red wine vinegar, 5g sugar, and 100ml water. Bring to a simmer until sugar dissolves. Pour hot brine over vegetable scraps in a heatproof jar. Cool completely. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour.

Cook Chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and black pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts for 6-8 minutes per side, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove from pan, rest for 5 minutes. Cut each breast into 2-3 substantial chunks.

Prepare Sauce: While chicken rests, finely dice the onion. Mince garlic cloves. In the same pan with residual chicken drippings, add remaining 15ml olive oil. Sauté onion until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic; cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Add the fermented tomatoes and their liquid. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 10-15 minutes, crushing tomatoes with a spoon, until sauce thickens slightly.
Cook Pasta: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add pasta and cook according to package instructions until al dente.

Combine: Roughly chop seasonal greens. Add greens to the tomato sauce; cook until just wilted, about 2-3 minutes. Drain pasta, reserving 60ml pasta water. Add drained pasta to the sauce. Add reserved pasta water if needed to achieve a desired consistency. Toss well to coat.
Serve: Divide pasta among 4 plates. Arrange chicken chunks alongside the pasta. Scatter pickled vegetable scraps and fresh torn basil over the dish. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust fermentation time for tomatoes based on desired level of tanginess and ambient temperature. Longer fermentation yields more sourness.
Any sturdy vegetable scraps can be used for pickling, such as broccoli stems, radish tops, or bell pepper cores.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Creamy Chicken with Mushrooms and Garlic Rice
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast, cut into two thick medallions, rests prominently on a clean white porcelain plate. Alongside, a neatly mounded portion of fluffy garlic rice. The chicken and rice are generously draped with a rich, creamy mushroom and sun-dried tomato sauce. Sautéed cremini mushrooms and halved cherry tomatoes are visible within the sauce, adding pops of earthy brown and vibrant red. The dish is garnished with finely chopped fresh basil, providing a contrasting green. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space. Served on a simple wooden table with a folded cotton napkin and classic silver flatware, under natural, even lighting, creating a warm bistro ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping
Pair with a dry white wine like Pinot Grigio or Chardonnay
instructions: Pat chicken medallions dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken. Set aside.

For garlic rice: Rinse rice. Combine 500ml water, 2 minced garlic cloves, and a pinch of salt in a saucepan. Bring to boil. Add rice. Reduce heat to low, cover. Simmer 15 minutes until water is absorbed. Fluff with fork.
In the same skillet, add remaining 15ml olive oil and butter. Add diced onion. Sauté 3 minutes until softened.
Add remaining 4 minced garlic cloves. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms. Cook 5-7 minutes until softened and browned. Add halved cherry tomatoes. Cook 2 minutes until slightly softened.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 3 minutes, scraping up browned bits.
Stir in heavy cream and grated Parmesan cheese. Simmer 2-3 minutes until sauce slightly thickens.
Return chicken medallions to skillet. Spoon sauce over chicken. Simmer 2 minutes to heat through.
Serve chicken with creamy mushroom sauce alongside garlic rice. Garnish with fresh chopped basil.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken and Potato Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty chicken and potato stew is presented in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The stew features two golden-brown chicken thighs, cooked until tender, nestled among substantial chunks of soft, pale yellow potatoes. Diced red tomatoes and translucent onion pieces are visible within the rich, savory, reddish-brown broth. The surface of the stew is lightly speckled with vibrant green chopped fresh parsley. The chicken skin is slightly crinkled, showing its slow-cooked texture. The broth has a natural, slightly viscous consistency, clinging to the ingredients. The bowl is placed slightly off-center on a simple, slightly worn, off-white ceramic plate. A simple fork and spoon rest beside the bowl. Warm, soft kitchen light illuminates the scene, highlighting the comforting textures and colors of the home-cooked meal.
instructions: Pat chicken dry. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, until golden brown, about 5-7 minutes. Flip. Sear other side 3 minutes. Remove chicken from pot.
Add chopped onions to pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes, chicken broth, dried thyme, and bay leaf. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Add potato chunks to pot. Return chicken to pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged in liquid.
Reduce heat to low. Cover pot. Simmer 30-40 minutes.
Cook until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and potatoes are tender.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Root Vegetable Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Chicken and Root Vegetable Rice is artfully mounded on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. The dish presents a harmonious blend of earthy tones and vibrant accents. Tender, diced chicken pieces are integrated throughout the creamy brown rice. Bright orange diced carrots and soft, pale yellow diced potatoes add color and texture. The rice has a rich, creamy consistency, reflecting the gradual absorption of broth. A generous sprinkle of freshly grated Parmesan cheese lightly dusts the top, melting subtly into the warmth. A vibrant scattering of fresh, finely chopped green parsley serves as a fresh garnish. The plate is positioned on a simple, light-toned wooden table, with a neatly folded white cotton napkin beside it. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting appeal. The background is clean and slightly blurred, suggesting a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Dice chicken thighs into 2cm pieces. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, deep pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken pieces. Sear chicken until browned on all sides. Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the pot. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced carrots and diced potatoes. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add brown rice to the pot. Stir well to coat rice with pan drippings and vegetables. Toast rice for 2 minutes.
Pour in 250ml of chicken broth. Stir constantly until liquid is mostly absorbed.

Continue adding broth, 250ml at a time. Stir frequently. Wait until each addition is nearly absorbed before adding the next. This process takes approximately 30-40 minutes, or until brown rice is tender.
Return cooked chicken to the pot. Stir to combine.
Remove pot from heat. Stir in grated Parmesan cheese and chopped fresh parsley. Mix until cheese is melted and creamy.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve immediately.
notes: Brown rice cooking times vary significantly by type. Adjust broth quantity and cooking duration as needed until the rice is tender but still has a slight bite.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Bacon, Potato & Cheddar Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of creamy pasta presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The pasta, such as rigatoni, is coated in a rich, pale yellow sauce. Interspersed throughout are golden-brown roasted potato chunks, approximately 2cm in size, showing slightly crisped edges. Scattered over the pasta are irregular pieces of crispy, dark reddish-brown bacon. Melted, grated sharp cheddar cheese lightly blankets sections of the dish, creating a glossy texture. Fresh, vibrant green basil leaves, some whole, some torn, are scattered over the top, providing a pop of color and freshness. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors. The plate is not overcrowded, allowing for moderate negative space.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Cut potatoes into 2cm chunks. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 25-30 minutes until golden and tender. Turn once during roasting.
Dice bacon into 1cm pieces. Cook bacon in a large skillet over medium heat until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Drain excess fat, leaving 15 ml in the skillet.
Cook pasta according to package directions in salted water until al dente. Drain, reserving 120 ml pasta water.
While pasta cooks, finely dice shallot and mince garlic. Add butter to the skillet with bacon fat. Sauté shallot until softened, about 3 minutes. Add garlic; cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth and heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce slightly thickens.
Add cooked pasta, roasted potato chunks, and crispy bacon to the sauce. Stir to combine. If needed, add reserved pasta water gradually to reach desired consistency.
Grate cheddar cheese. Stir half of the grated cheddar into the pasta mixture until melted and creamy. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Divide pasta among serving plates. Top each portion with remaining grated cheddar. Garnish generously with fresh basil leaves, some whole, some torn.

recipes.recipe_name: Panang Chocolate Chicken with Cherry Walnut Relish
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Panang Chocolate Chicken is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A thick, seared chicken thigh, cooked to a rich golden-brown exterior, rests centrally. A luscious, glossy reddish-brown Panang chocolate sauce pools around the chicken, with some gently spooned over the top. The sauce is smooth with a subtle sheen. A vibrant mound of cherry walnut relish is artfully placed beside the chicken, showcasing roughly chopped toasted walnuts and plump, quartered dried cherries, flecked with bright green cilantro. The colors are earthy and warm, with the deep reds of the sauce and cherries contrasting with the golden chicken and green herbs. The plate has moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table surface and a white cotton napkin placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish. A Thai-style spoon and fork are placed alongside the plate, completing the culturally authentic table setting.

ingredients.name: Dark chocolate (70% cacao or higher), finely chopped

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer chicken to a plate. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add Panang curry paste to the skillet. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in coconut milk and chicken stock. Stir well to combine with the paste. Bring to a simmer.
Add chopped dark chocolate, fish sauce, and brown sugar. Stir until chocolate melts and sauce is smooth.
Return chicken thighs to the skillet. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Turn chicken once halfway through.
While chicken simmers, prepare the relish. Roughly chop dried cherries and toasted walnuts. In a small bowl, combine chopped cherries, walnuts, fresh cilantro, and lime juice. Mix well.
Taste the sauce. Adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve chicken thighs with Panang chocolate sauce. Top generously with the cherry walnut relish.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Short Ribs with Potato and White Bean Ragout
recipes.visual_description: A single, generously portioned braised beef short rib sits centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The short rib is dark, rich brown, deeply caramelized, presented as a whole, unsliced chunk. Beneath and around it, a savory ragout of golden-brown roasted potato cubes and creamy white cannellini beans is neatly spooned. The beans and potatoes are coated in a glossy, rich, dark amber braising sauce, thick enough to cling. A sprinkle of bright green, freshly chopped flat-leaf parsley garnishes the dish. The plate rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors, creating an inviting, sophisticated yet approachable presentation.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
Pat short ribs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear short ribs on all sides until deeply browned. Remove ribs.
Add diced onions, carrots, and celery to the Dutch oven. Sauté 8-10 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes, stirring.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up browned bits from the bottom. Simmer 5 minutes until reduced by half.
Stir in beef broth, thyme, and bay leaves. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared short ribs to the Dutch oven. Liquid should mostly cover ribs. Add more broth if needed.
Cover Dutch oven. Transfer to preheated oven. Braise 2.5-3 hours, or until ribs are very tender.
While ribs braise, prepare potatoes. Toss potato cubes with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Spread potatoes on a baking sheet. Roast in the same oven during the last 45 minutes of braising, or roast separately at 200°C for 25-30 minutes until golden and tender.
Once ribs are tender, remove them from Dutch oven. Set aside, covered.
Strain braising liquid through a fine-mesh sieve into a saucepan. Discard solids.
Skim fat from braising liquid. Bring liquid to a simmer over medium-high heat. Reduce until slightly thickened, about 10-15 minutes.
Add drained cannellini beans to the reduced sauce. Simmer 5 minutes.
Gently stir in roasted potato cubes. Season ragout with salt and pepper.
Serve braised short ribs over the potato and white bean ragout. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Spanish Tortilla
recipes.visual_description: A thick, golden-brown Classic Spanish Tortilla sits centrally on a simple, round ceramic plate. The tortilla is round, with rustic, slightly uneven edges, showcasing its home-cooked nature. Its surface is a rich golden brown, indicating a perfectly cooked crust. A cross-section reveals a moist, tender interior, pale yellow in color, with visible, soft slices of potato and translucent, caramelized onion pieces embedded throughout. The texture is invitingly soft inside with a firm exterior. A few flecks of chopped fresh parsley are sprinkled over the top. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table. Adjacent to the plate, a simple, rustic fork and a casually folded cloth napkin complete the homely setting. The lighting is warm and cozy, suggestive of a family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve at room temperature or slightly warm.
Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
Cut into wedges for individual portions.
instructions: Peel potatoes. Slice into thin medallions, about 2-3mm thick. Peel onion. Slice thinly.
Heat olive oil in a 20cm non-stick frying pan over medium-low heat. Add sliced potatoes and onion. Ensure they are submerged in oil.
Cook slowly for 20-25 minutes. Potatoes and onions should be very tender, almost confit, but not browned. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
Carefully drain almost all olive oil from the pan, reserving about 2 tablespoons in the pan. Transfer cooked potatoes and onions to a large bowl.
Crack eggs into the bowl with potatoes and onions. Season generously with salt and pepper. Gently mix to combine, mashing some potato slices slightly.
Return the pan with reserved oil to medium heat. Pour the egg and potato mixture into the hot pan. Spread evenly.
Cook for 5-7 minutes. Edges should set and turn golden. Center should still be slightly soft.
Place a large plate over the pan. Invert the pan to flip the tortilla onto the plate. Slide the tortilla back into the pan, uncooked side down.
Cook for another 3-5 minutes until golden brown and set through. Internal temperature should reach 75°C (167°F).
Slide the tortilla onto a serving plate. Let it rest for a few minutes before slicing.
traditional_techniques: Confit-style frying of potatoes and onions in olive oil
Flipping the tortilla using a plate

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken, Mushroom, and Potato Gratin
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Creamy Chicken, Mushroom, and Potato Gratin presented in a white oval gratin dish, placed on a simple wooden table. The gratin features a golden-brown, bubbly crust of melted mozzarella and thinly sliced, roasted potatoes. Beneath the crust, layers of tender, 3cm chicken chunks, sautéed mushrooms, and creamy brown rice are visible, bathed in a rich, savory sauce. A few fresh thyme sprigs are casually placed on top for garnish, adding a touch of vibrant green. The dish exhibits a harmonious blend of textures—crispy edges, soft interior, and slightly chewy rice. The overall presentation is professional yet comforting, with natural, even lighting highlighting the inviting warmth and rich colors of the dish. A folded white cotton napkin rests beside the dish, creating a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Cook brown rice according to package directions. Set aside.
Peel and thinly slice potatoes into 2-3 mm rounds. Set aside.
Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large oven-safe pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Do not cook through. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add remaining 1 tbsp olive oil to the pan. Add chopped onion and sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are tender and browned, about 7-8 minutes.
Melt butter in the pan. Sprinkle flour over vegetables. Stir for 1 minute to create a roux.
Gradually whisk in chicken broth and heavy cream. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens. Season with salt, pepper, and fresh thyme leaves.
Add seared chicken chunks back into the sauce. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Lightly grease a 23x33 cm (9x13 inch) baking dish.
Spread half of the cooked brown rice evenly on the bottom of the baking dish.
Arrange half of the thinly sliced potatoes over the rice.
Pour half of the chicken and mushroom sauce mixture over the potatoes.
Repeat layers with remaining brown rice, potatoes, and chicken-mushroom sauce.
Top evenly with shredded mozzarella cheese.
Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until potatoes are tender, cheese is golden and bubbly, and chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Soy-Ginger Glazed Chicken with Sesame Brown Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple light wooden table surface. A moderate portion of fluffy, light brown sesame brown rice forms a neat mound on one side of the plate. Adjacent to the rice are several irregularly shaped, glistening pieces of dark golden-brown chicken thigh, coated generously in a rich, glossy soy-ginger glaze. The chicken pieces are tender and plump, showing no fanning or slicing. Bright green, tender-crisp steamed broccoli florets are thoughtfully arranged around the chicken and rice, providing a vibrant color contrast. A sprinkle of white toasted sesame seeds adorns the chicken and rice, adding texture and a subtle sheen. Thinly sliced vibrant green spring onion pieces are scattered over the dish, providing freshness. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with appropriate negative space. Beside the plate, a pair of dark wooden chopsticks rests on a small ceramic chopstick rest. A folded grey cotton napkin is placed to the side. Natural, even light illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and colors of the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small dish of pickled ginger or a light clear broth on the side.
instructions: Rinse brown rice thoroughly. Combine rice and 600ml water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 40-45 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Let stand covered for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork. Stir in 5ml sesame oil.
While rice cooks, prepare the glaze. In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, grated ginger, minced garlic, and remaining 5ml sesame oil.
In another small bowl, dissolve cornstarch in 30ml cold water to create a slurry.

Heat vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan or wok over medium-high heat. Add chicken thigh pieces, cut into 4cm pieces. Sear chicken for 5-7 minutes, turning occasionally, until browned on all sides. Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan.
Add the prepared glaze to the pan. Bring to a simmer. Stir in cornstarch slurry. Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens to a glossy consistency.
Return cooked chicken to the pan. Toss to coat evenly with the glaze.
Steam broccoli florets until tender-crisp, about 3-5 minutes.

To plate, spoon a portion of sesame brown rice onto a white porcelain dinner plate. Arrange glazed chicken chunks beside the rice. Place steamed broccoli florets around the chicken. Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and sliced spring onions.

recipes.recipe_name: Panang Chicken Curry with Dark Chocolate and Cherries
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Panang Chicken Curry is presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl, centered on a simple wooden table surface. The rich, reddish-brown curry is glossy, with tender thick chunks of chicken visibly nestled within. Vibrant red and green bell pepper strips add contrasting color and texture. Dark, plump dried cherries and light brown, roughly chopped walnuts are scattered throughout the creamy sauce, creating visual interest. A generous scattering of fresh, bright green basil leaves provides a final aromatic garnish. Beside the bowl, a portion of fluffy white jasmine rice is neatly mounded. A traditional Thai-style serving spoon rests on the table next to the bowl. A clean cotton napkin is folded beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, highlighting the dish as the focal point within a casual bistro atmosphere. The background is minimal and unobtrusive, ensuring full attention remains on the well-balanced and professionally plated curry.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice
Offer additional fish sauce or chili flakes on the side for personal seasoning
instructions: Prepare jasmine rice according to package directions.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or wok over medium heat. Add Panang curry paste. Stir-fry for 2 minutes until fragrant and oil separates.
Pour in 200ml coconut milk. Stir constantly until a red sheen appears.
Add chicken pieces. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until chicken is seared.
Pour in remaining 600ml coconut milk. Add kaffir lime leaves. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Stir in fish sauce and palm sugar. Simmer for 10 minutes, or until chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Add red and green bell pepper thick strips. Cook for 3-4 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Stir in chopped dark chocolate and dried cherries. Cook 1 minute until chocolate melts.
Remove from heat. Stir in roughly chopped walnuts.
Serve hot with jasmine rice. Garnish with fresh basil leaves.
traditional_techniques: Stir-frying curry paste until oil separates (Phad Prik Gaeng)

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of creamy, free-flowing risotto is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto is a warm, pale yellow hue, studded with tender, golden-brown seared chicken cubes (2cm) and sautéed earthy brown mushroom slices. Finely diced onion pieces are visible throughout the creamy rice. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley garnishes the top, alongside delicate shavings of Parmesan cheese. The dish has a natural, organic arrangement, showcasing its rich texture. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, with classic silver Italian flatware (fork and spoon) placed beside it, and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a softly blurred modern bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread.
Pair with a light Italian white wine.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 2cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pot or deep pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken cubes until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken and set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil and 15g butter to the same pot.
Sauté finely diced onion until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are tender and browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in Arborio rice. Toast rice for 2 minutes, ensuring all grains are coated.
Pour in white wine. Stir constantly until wine is fully absorbed.
Add one ladleful (about 250ml) of hot chicken broth. Stir continuously until liquid is absorbed.
Continue adding broth, one ladleful at a time. Stir constantly and wait for each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 20-25 minutes.
When rice is creamy and al dente, stir in cooked chicken.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 15g butter and grated Parmesan cheese.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and extra shaved Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Biryani
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken Biryani served on a clean white porcelain plate. The dish features a mound of long-grain Basmati rice. The rice displays a natural color variation from pale white to deep orange-yellow from the spice infusion. Two large, bone-in chicken thigh chunks are nestled within the rice. The chicken is tender and coated in a thick, savory masala. Topping the rice are thin, golden-brown fried onion strips and vibrant green sprigs of fresh coriander. The arrangement is organic and centered with moderate negative space. A small ceramic bowl of white yogurt raita sits to the side. The background is a dark wood bistro table with a folded linen napkin and a polished brass spoon.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of cucumber raita
Accompany with lime wedges and sliced raw red onions
Traditional brass or copper serving spoon

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs, bone-in, cut into large chunks

instructions: Wash rice until water runs clear. Soak in water for 30 minutes.
Mix chicken chunks with yogurt, spice mix, ginger-garlic paste, and 5g salt. Marinate for 1 hour.
Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pot. Fry sliced onions until dark golden brown. Remove half for garnish.
Boil 1.5 L water with 10g salt. Add soaked rice. Cook until 70% tender. Drain immediately.
Add marinated chicken to the pot with remaining onions and ghee. Cook for 5 minutes over medium heat.
Layer the parboiled rice over the chicken chunks. Top with reserved fried onions, coriander, and mint.
Cover pot with a tight-fitting lid. Use a heavy weight or dough to seal steam inside.
Cook on very low heat for 25 minutes. Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Turn off heat. Let the pot rest for 10 minutes before opening.
Gently fluff the rice from the sides to mix colors without breaking grains.
notes: Do not overcook the rice during the initial boil or it will turn mushy during the steaming phase.
Use a heavy-bottomed pot (like a Dutch oven) to prevent the bottom layer of chicken from burning.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Coconut Tomato Pasta with Roasted Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, contemporary pasta dish presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Long strands of fettuccine are generously coated in a creamy, reddish-orange sauce, a harmonious blend of rich tomato and subtle coconut. Scattered throughout the pasta are tender, vibrant green roasted broccoli florets, some with lightly charred edges, and burst cherry tomatoes, their skins slightly wrinkled from roasting. The composition is organic and flowing, with elements intertwined rather than rigidly arranged, allowing for natural negative space. A garnish of fresh, torn green basil leaves is delicately placed on top, adding a pop of fresh color and aroma. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by modern silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and inviting colors, creating an approachable yet refined restaurant-style presentation.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss broccoli florets and cherry tomatoes with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking tray. Roast for 15-20 minutes, until tender and slightly charred. Set aside.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120 ml pasta water before draining. Drain pasta.
While pasta cooks, heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a large deep pan or pot over medium heat. Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, coconut milk, and vegetable broth. Add red pepper flakes if using. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce slightly thickens.
Add cooked pasta to the sauce. Toss to coat evenly. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, 30 ml at a time, until desired consistency is reached.
Gently fold in roasted broccoli and cherry tomatoes. Stir in fresh basil.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed. Serve immediately.
